items.title: Germany backs Ukraine's Zelenskiy after Trump's call for his removal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks.
items.body:
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks.
Wadephul said Germany remained by the side of Ukraine and its government "and fully support the President as he carries out his difficult duties."
The comments, at a leadership meeting of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), followed Trump's call on Saturday for Zelenskiy to be replaced and underlined Berlin's growing rift with Washington.
Trump, who last week announced a diesel supply deal with Russia, called for Ukraine to [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"replace Zelenskiy"] and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure.
Germany, the biggest European donor to Ukraine, said on Saturday it would [USN:L1N45W02N TEXT:"maintain sanctions"] against Russia despite Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel.
Wadephul, who met his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month, said "consistency and clarity" were needed to support Ukraine and bring Moscow to negotiate.
"We don't need less pressure, we need more pressure on Putin to make him be ready to negotiate," Wadephul said. "That is what this moment requires and that's what the government stands for."
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskiy [USN:FWN45V15A TEXT:"on Saturday"] and told him the UK would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia, a Downing Street spokesperson said.

items.title: Deutsche Bank chief warns German election results worrying foreign investors
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes.
items.body:
The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes.
The AfD, which wants to restrict immigration and send asylum seekers home, scored some of its biggest-ever wins in eastern Germany last month. At the same time, the Left Party scored its biggest win in the election for the city government of Berlin, pledging to [USN:L1N45C05W TEXT:"expropriate holdings"] of property companies.
"This poses a significant risk to Germany, and it should not be played down," Christian Sewing, chief executive of Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) , told the Bild daily in an interview, referring to the rise of political extremes.
"You can't expect a foreign investor to immediately draw a distinction between a state government and Germany as a whole," he said. "It's seen as Germany as a whole and I think that from an investor's point of view, that's understandable."
In the state of Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD, which is classified by security services as extremist in some regions, only narrowly fell short of an [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"absolute majority"] in the state parliament, and it followed up two weeks later by taking first place in [USN:L1N45C01D TEXT:"Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania"].
The AfD has been accused by economists of fostering a climate that will drive away badly needed skilled workers and foreign investors.
The Left Party, meanwhile, vowed to tackle Berlin's soaring housing costs by [USN:L8N45D1DV TEXT:"expropriating the holdings"] of residential property companies.
"And whether it's Saxony-Anhalt with the AfD or what's happening here in Berlin, it's anything but conducive to economic growth. And it's anything but investment-friendly," Sewing said.
He urged the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz to carry on with reforms to revive the economy.
"That is the only response we have to the far-right and far-left extremists in this country," he said.

NEW DELHI: Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day on Sunday (Oct 11) as sporadic protests broke out demanding India's election chief quit, and a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
Dipke and the other Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
The court ordered their release with an undertaking to "maintain public peace", the CJP said in a statement.
"Cockroaches never die," the group posted on its X account shortly after Dipke's release.

Youth protesters, many of them from student organisations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests around the city on Sunday afternoon before police detained them and hauled them away in vehicles.
The All India Students' Association alleged in a post on X that those detained were assaulted by police inside the vehicles.

Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) talk after their release at Delhi Cantt Police Station in New Delhi, India, Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Priyanshu Singh)

A video posted on X by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) showed one of its lawmakers, John Brittas, being helped from a bus to an autorickshaw as he appeared to be in distress.
Reuters could not verify claims about detainees being assaulted by police.
The Delhi Police spokesperson did not respond to calls made by Reuters to seek comment.
The youth movement is one of the biggest political challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his 12 years in power, during which his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has repeatedly swept the polls and eliminated any serious challenge by opponents, including the Congress Party.
The protesters are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi.

items.title: Zelenski dice que Ucrania cesará ataques a refinerías si Rusia deja en paz su sistema de energía
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ucrania está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas si Moscú pone fin al bombardeo de la infraestructura energética ucraniana, dijo el domingo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, exigió a Kiev un cese unilateral.
items.body:
Ucrania está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas si Moscú pone fin al bombardeo de la infraestructura energética ucraniana, dijo el domingo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski, después de que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, exigió a Kiev un cese unilateral.
Trump culpó el sábado a los ataques ucranianos contra las refinerías rusas del aumento de los precios del diésel en Estados Unidos y dijo que a Zelenski "más le vale dejar de hacerlo", además sostuvo que Ucrania debería sustituirlo como líder porque había desperdiciado varias oportunidades para llegar a un acuerdo con Moscú.
La fuerte subida de los precios mundiales del diésel, tras el estallido de la guerra de Irán en febrero, se ha convertido en un lastre político para el Partido Republicano de Trump antes de las elecciones legislativas del próximo mes, en las que los demócratas de la oposición podrían hacerse con el control de una o ambas cámaras del Congreso.
Zelenski reiteró el domingo la postura que Ucrania mantiene desde hace tiempo: que está dispuesta a detener los ataques contra las refinerías rusas únicamente como parte de una desescalada mutua del conflicto, lo que requeriría que Moscú cese sus propios ataques contra las infraestructuras energéticas ucranianas.
Cualquier acuerdo de este tipo tendría que ir acompañado de "garantías reales", dijo Zelenskiy.
"La verdadera causa de la guerra en Europa es Rusia y solo Rusia", dijo Zelenskiy, sin aludir específicamente a las declaraciones de Trump. "Es posible detener los ataques contra las infraestructuras energéticas ya desde hoy mismo, pero Putin no quiere hacerlo".
El sábado, Zelenski respondió airadamente al anuncio de Trump sobre un acuerdo de suministro de gasóleo con Rusia, que, según él, alentaría los ataques de Moscú contra Ucrania.
Analistas dijeron que es poco probable que el acuerdo de Trump con Moscú resulte en una baja sostenida de los precios del combustible, ya que los volúmenes siguen siendo muy inferiores a los que Rusia suele exportar cuando sus refinerías no están bajo ataque.
El acuerdo sobre el gasóleo también fue criticado por legisladores estadounidenses, entre ellos uno de los compañeros republicanos de Trump, el diputado Don Bacon, quien dijo que era el momento de aplicar más sanciones, no de levantarlas.
En las calles de Kiev, varios residentes expresaron su indignación ante la sugerencia de Trump de que Ucrania debería buscar un nuevo líder dispuesto a llegar a un acuerdo con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin.
"Nadie tiene derecho a decirnos qué hacer, sobre todo porque no se pueden tener elecciones en tiempo de guerra", dijo Sabina, una profesora de primaria de 40 años, refiriéndose a la prohibición de comicios en Ucrania bajo la ley marcial por razones de seguridad.
"En mi opinión, es una traición por parte de nuestros socios", añadió sobre las declaraciones de Trump.

WARSAW: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday (Oct 11) after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.
Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not go into details but authorities were treating the threat as "deadly serious".
"We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out," he told reporters.
Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security.
While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.
In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.
In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

Source: Reuters/cy

items.title: Mueren 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, en naufragio entre Yibuti a Yemen: agencia de la ONU
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Al menos 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, fallecieron y más de 116 están desaparecidos tras el naufragio de una embarcación que transportaba a unas 305 personas desde Yibuti a Yemen, informó el domingo la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) de las Naciones Unidas.
items.body:
Al menos 109 migrantes, entre ellos 15 niños, fallecieron y más de 116 están desaparecidos tras el naufragio de una embarcación que transportaba a unas 305 personas desde Yibuti a Yemen, informó el domingo la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) de las Naciones Unidas.
La embarcación zozobró cerca de Guhere, al norte de la ciudad portuaria yibutiana de Obock, durante la noche del 8 al 9 de octubre, según la OIM, que recabó testimonios de los supervivientes.
Más de 80 personas sobrevivieron al naufragio, todas ellas de nacionalidad etíope, según el comunicado. Un portavoz del Gobierno etíope no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios.
De los 109 cadáveres recuperados tras el naufragio, 52 son hombres, 42 mujeres y 15 niños, según la OIM.
"Nuestros equipos se encuentran sobre el terreno junto a las autoridades locales para prestar asistencia de emergencia", dijo Alexandre Coissac, jefe de misión de la OIM en Yibuti.
"Esta tragedia es un claro recordatorio de los peligros a los que se enfrentan los migrantes en este corredor migratorio en su búsqueda de oportunidades económicas", añadió Coissac.
Las autoridades de Yibuti continúan con las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, según el comunicado de la OIM, que añadió que las autoridades locales también están prestando asistencia médica a los supervivientes y organizando los entierros de los fallecidos.
No fue posible contactar de inmediato con el Gobierno de Yibuti para recabar sus comentarios.
Yemen está viviendo la escalada más grave de los combates entre las fuerzas gubernamentales respaldadas por Arabia Saudita y los hutíes, apoyados por Irán, desde que una tregua negociada por la ONU detuvo en gran medida los ataques transfronterizos en 2022.
La reanudación del conflicto podría redefinir el control en Yemen, con repercusiones para las rutas marítimas del mar Rojo.
La OIM calificó de alarmante la crisis desencadenada por los combates, con cifras de desplazados que se han disparado de 76 000 a 200 000 desde mediados de septiembre, según datos publicados por la OIM la semana pasada.
Más de 3.700 personas han huido de Yemen por mar hacia Yibuti hasta la semana pasada, según la OIM.
El mes pasado también estallaron combates en Etiopía, en lo que supone la mayor escalada de violencia desde la guerra de Tigray.

items.body:
El huracán Simón se convertirá en uno de gran intensidad el domingo, cerca de la costa centrooccidental de México, y se acercará mucho a la ribera el lunes, pronosticó el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (CNH) de Estados Unidos.
Simon se encontraba a unos 96.56 kilometros al oeste suroeste de Manzanillo a primera hora de la mañana del domingo, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 250 kilómetros, según la última actualización del CNH.

items.title: Arsenal forward Russo voted as England women's player of the year
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Forward Alessia Russo has been voted by fans as England women's player of the year for the 2025-26 season, winning the award for the second time in her career, the national team announced on Sunday.
items.body:
Forward Alessia Russo has been voted by fans as England women's player of the year for the 2025-26 season, winning the award for the second time in her career, the national team announced on Sunday.
Arsenal player Russo, who also won the award in 2023-24, was the most prolific English scorer in the Women's Super League last season with 13 goals and six assists. Her double in a 3-0 win over Aston Villa in May helped Arsenal secure Champions League qualification.
The 27-year-old also played a leading role in England's World Cup qualification campaign, starting in all six group matches and scoring three times.
"To receive the award is really special, particularly as it comes directly from the fans," said Russo, who beat Lucy Bronze and Hannah Hampton in the poll.
"I absolutely love playing for England every moment I get... hopefully we will go on to have a really big season."
Russo was on the scoresheet when England beat Greece 3-1 in their World Cup round one playoff tie on Friday, with the reverse fixture set for Tuesday in Leicester.

items.title: Le pape Léon va être opéré d'un nodule au poumon
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le pape Léon a déclaré dimanche que les médecins avaient détecté une petite excroissance pulmonaire lors d'un récent examen de santé et qu'il subirait une intervention chirurgicale cette semaine pour la retirer.
items.body:
Le pape Léon a déclaré dimanche que les médecins avaient détecté une petite excroissance pulmonaire lors d'un récent examen de santé et qu'il subirait une intervention chirurgicale cette semaine pour la retirer.
Âgé de 71 ans, Léon a déclaré aux pèlerins réunis sur la place Saint-Pierre à l'occasion de sa prière dominicale hebdomadaire que cette excroissance était circonscrite et avait été détectée à un stade précoce.
"Récemment, à l'occasion de certains examens, les médecins ont trouvé un nodule circonscrit au poumon. Il a été détecté à un stade très précoce et est bien localisé", a déclaré le souverain pontife.
"Les médecins estiment qu'il convient d'intervenir et, suivant leurs conseils, j'ai décidé de subir une intervention chirurgicale pour le retirer", a-t-il déclaré.
"Cette intervention est déjà programmée dans les prochains jours."
Le bureau de presse du Vatican a précisé que la convalescence du pape après l'opération devrait durer environ une semaine.

items.title: El papa León se someterá a una cirugía para extirpar un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo.
items.body:
El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo.
León, de 71 años, explicó a los peregrinos reunidos en la Plaza de San Pedro para su oración dominical semanal que el nódulo estaba "bien localizado" y se había detectado a tiempo, y les pidió que oraran "por la visita pastoral que voy a realizar" a Uruguay, Argentina y Perú.
"Recientemente, durante unos exámenes médicos, los médicos encontraron un nódulo localizado en mi pulmón", dijo el pontífice. "Se detectó en una fase muy temprana y está bien localizado".
"Los médicos consideran aconsejable intervenir, por lo que, siguiendo su consejo, he decidido someterme a una intervención quirúrgica para extirparlo", añadió. "La operación ya está programada para los próximos días".
Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. Según la Sociedad Torácica Americana, menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores.
Leo, elegido papa por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es más joven de lo usual para ser jefe de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, entre ellos el tenis, y no se tiene constancia de que haya tenido problemas de salud antes.
Su predecesor, el difunto papa Francisco, falleció a los 88 años y se encontraba cada vez más débil en sus últimos años.
La oficina de prensa del Vaticano indicó que se esperaba que la recuperación de Leo tras la intervención quirúrgica durara aproximadamente una semana. No facilitó de inmediato más detalles sobre el estado de salud del papa.
Leo tiene una agenda muy apretada y tiene previsto realizar una gira de 11 días por Uruguay, Argentina y Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre.

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo said on Sunday (Oct 11) that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
Pope Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.
The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant.
"Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localised nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."

"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days."
A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5 per cent of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size and other factors such as smoking.
Pope Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.

Related:

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well.
"I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement.
"The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it during today’s Angelus are reassuring," Meloni added.
The late Pope Francis, Pope Leo's predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.
The Vatican press office said the pope's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health.
Pope Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17.
Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake".

Source: Reuters/fh

VATICAN CITY, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff’s tenure.

Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter’s Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was “well-contained” and caught at an early stage.

“Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung,” said the pontiff. “It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained.”

“The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it,” he said. “The operation is already scheduled for the next few days.”

Leo, elected pope by the world’s cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to previously have had health issues.

The late Pope Francis, Leo’s predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.

The Vatican press office said Leo’s recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope’s health.

items.title: ローマ教皇、肺に小さなしこり　数日以内に手術へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] - ローマ教皇レオ１４世（７１）は１２日、先の健康診断で肺に小さなしこりが見つかり、今週中に切除手術を受けると明らかにした。２０２５年５月の就任後、健康問題が明らかになるのは初めて。

バチカンのサンピエトロ広場で行った日曜恒例の祈りの集いで信者らに説明した。しこりは局所的なもので、ごく早期に発見されたという。

教皇は「（医師の）助言に従い、切除手術を受けることを決めた」と述べた。手術は数日以内に予定されているという。

レオ１４世は７１歳と教皇としては比較的若く、テニスなどのスポーツを好む。これまで大きな健康問題は知られていなかった。前任のフランシスコ教皇は晩年、健康状態が悪化し、８８歳で死去した。

バチカン報道官室によると、レオ１４世は術後１週間程度で回復する見通し。健康状態について、それ以上の詳細は明らかにしていない。

items.title: Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
items.body:
Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.
The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant.
"Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."
"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days."
A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.
"Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital.
"When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said.
LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well.
"I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement.
"The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added.
The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health.
The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health.
Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17.
Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide, 5 missing

By Gopal Sharma
KATHMANDU, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.

Two women and three men were out of contact, the national disaster authority said. The army said a further 49 people, including a foreigner, had been rescued. They did not give the person’s nationality.

A landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said.

Show Full Article

The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.

“We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe,” said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district’s most senior bureaucrat.

The flood swept away about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.

The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.

National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood.

“Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed,” the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post.

Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

(Reporting by Gopal Sharma; Editing by Jamie Freed and Kate Mayberry)

WARSAW, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, an Interior Ministry spokesperson said on X.

The exact nature of the threat and its origin were not immediately clear.

“Following information received by the Polish Police regarding a possible attack …Interior Minister, Marcin Kierwiński, and the Minister-Coordinator of Special Services, Tomasz Siemoniak, have ordered action to be taken in this matter,” spokesperson Karolina Galecka wrote.

Show Full Article

“A meeting will be held today at 11:00 a.m. at the Internal Security Agency’s Counter-Terrorism Centre.”

A spokesperson for the minister-coordinator of special services said he had no further comment.

Private broadcaster Radio Zet reported that police had received an email with information about the threat.

While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.

In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.

In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

Sunday’s announcement came as authorities in Poland have been on high alert following a wave of violence in schools that resulted in the death of a caretaker on Thursday.

(Reporting by Alan CharlishEditing by Tomasz Janowski and Christina Fincher)

items.title: フーシ派、サウジ空港・領空は「作戦区域」　軍事作戦に報復警告
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jana Choukeir　Maha El Dahan　Timour Azhari

［ドバイ／リヤド　１１日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Jana Choukeir　Maha El Dahan　Timour Azhari

［ドバイ／リヤド　１１日　ロイター］ - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１１日、航空会社や旅行者、空港関係者に対し、サウジアラビア国内の空港に近づかないよう警告した。サウジがイエメンで軍事行動を続ければ、さらに強い対応を招くと主張した。

１０日には首都リヤドの国際空港が攻撃を受け、少なくとも１２人が死亡し、３００人余りが負傷。トランプ米大統領は、サウジの対フーシ派軍事作戦に参加するか「検討」する考えを示した。

フーシ派はＸへの投稿で「全ての航空会社、専門家、従業員、労働者、旅行者に対し、サウジの空港と領空を使用しないよう改めて警告する。（聖地である）メッカとメディナの空港を除き、サウジの空港と領空は攻撃に対して脆弱（ぜいじゃく）であり、われわれの作戦部隊の作戦区域となっている」と表明。「迎撃に失敗した場合の責任はサウジ側にある」とした。

フーシ派の「外務省」は１１日、「サウジという敵がイエメンへの侵略と干渉をやめなければ、さらに悪い事態が訪れるだろう」と述べた。フーシ派系メディアが伝えた。

１０日のリヤドの空港に対する攻撃は過去１週間で３回目。死者は、サウジ人が４人、バングラデシュ人２人のほか、米国、ヨルダン、パレスチナ、シリア、スーダン、エジプト国籍の人が含まれている。

航空当局は、被害状況と安全性の評価を行うため空港業務を一時停止したと発表した。再開時期は示していない。

サウジ主導の連合軍は１０日、サウジ東部ダンマームのキング・ファハド国際空港付近にも飛翔体が落下したと発表した。１１日も同地域で無人機（ドローン）１機を迎撃したと明らかにした。

サウジのエネルギー省は、世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は予定通り１１日からリヤドで開催されると発表した。この会合は空港から約１０キロメートルの施設で１１─１５日の日程で開催される。国営テレビによると、閣僚７０人以上、企業幹部３００人、国際エネルギー機関２５団体以上の代表者が出席する予定だ。

items.title: HSBC leads international banks in financing India Inc across debt, equity
items.author: Subrata Panda
items.summary: The bank topped G3 bonds and syndicated loans, and ranked among the leading international investment banks for equity fundraising ...
items.body: London-headquartered HSBC emerged as the leading international bank facilitating fundraising by Indian companies through G3 bonds, syndicated loans and initial public offerings (IPOs) in January-September 2026, leveraging its extensive corporate and institutional relationships and its ability to connect borrowers with pools of capital seeking investment opportunities across debt and equity markets. The bank moved up from third place in G3 bonds last year, retained its lead in syndicated loans for the third consecutive year and ranked second among international investment banks for primary equity fundraising through IPOs and qualified institutional placements (QIPs) since January 2025. “Our financing business spans three markets: loans, bonds and equity, including IPOs and QIPs. From January 1 to September 30, we were number one in syndicated loans, with the largest market share. This includes financing for companies making overseas acquisitions, funding capex, refinancing or retiring rupee loans, and meeting other funding needs. We also hold the largest market share in G3 bonds, based on total volume raised by banks locally. In equity, we are number one in IPOs and number two in QIPs,” Hitendra Dave, chief executive officer of HSBC India, told Business Standard. Dave attributed the bank’s strength in financing to its access to corporates and institutions, including banks, and its ability to identify pools of capital seeking investment opportunities across bonds, loans and equities. HSBC was also among the leading banks in mobilising FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) concessional swap window, raising $14.5 billion between June and August. It ranked second to ICICI Bank, which mobilised nearly $18 billion. Banks collectively raised nearly $133 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the facility. Dave attributed HSBC’s mobilisation to its strong non-resident Indian (NRI) franchise and presence across global markets. “I don’t want HSBC to be strong only in financing. We want to build the business in a way that puts us far ahead of the competition. In areas such as wealth, local banks are doing better than us. But our ambition is to be number one or number two in every segment we operate in, and at least in the top three where that isn’t possible,” Dave said. HSBC’s debt-market performance was reflected in its transaction mandates. According to Bloomberg data, the bank topped India’s G3 bond league table in January-September 2026, moving up from third place last year. It also ranked as the leading bookrunner for syndicated loans originating in India for the third consecutive year, with a 21 per cent share of total volumes, according to Dealogic. In the G3 bond market, HSBC worked on a $1 billion dual-tranche offering by Export-Import Bank of India, a $750 million bond sale by the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), and a $1 billion issue by ICICI Bank. Its other mandates included a $700 million offering by Bank of Baroda and a $600 million bond sale by renewable energy company ReNew Power. India’s G3 bond issuance reached $21.8 billion by late September, nearly four times the $5.54 billion raised in all of 2025 and approaching the previous annual record of about $22.4 billion. In syndicated lending, HSBC arranged a $100 million rupee-denominated acquisition financing for Waaree RTL on a sole basis, following the RBI’s liberalisation of onshore acquisition-financing regulations. Other mandates included a $125 million debut syndicated loan for RateGain to support a cross-border strategic acquisition and an $85 million, seven-year syndicated term loan for Piramal Pharma to finance cross-border capital expenditure, with repayments aligned to projected cash flows. The bank also arranged $1 billion in financing for A V Minerals (Novelis) to meet cross-border funding requirements and secured mandates for $450 million across three transactions for Bank of Maharashtra. HSBC attributed its position in syndicated lending to its first-mover advantage in novel financing structures and its status as a preferred lender for large Indian corporates undertaking acquisitions. In equity capital markets, HSBC completed six IPOs worth about $5 billion in January-September 2026 and led four of the five largest offerings during the period, accounting for 84 per cent of their combined deal value, according to the bank. It was present in the three largest IPOs identified by HSBC: Jio’s $4 billion offering, the National Stock Exchange’s $2.4 billion offering and SBI Funds Management’s $1.3 billion offering. HSBC said it was leading eight of the 12 largest forthcoming IPOs, including those of Jio Platforms, Avaada Electro, Zetwerk and AGS Eye. Additionally, the bank facilitated fundraising by Indian companies through QIPs, including State Bank of India’s $2.9 billion offering, JSW Infrastructure’s $794 million offering and Biocon’s $460 million QIP.

items.title: 109 migrants, including 15 children dead after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, have died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying about 305 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
items.body:
At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, have died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying about 305 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
The boat capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of 8–9 October, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts.
More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals, the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Among the 109 bodies recovered after the boat capsized, 52 are men, 42 women and 15 children including nine girls and six boys, the IOM said.
"Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac.
"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said.
Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased.
The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment.
Yemen is [USN:L6N45T0PU TEXT:"experiencing"] the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. The renewed conflict could reshape control in Yemen, with implications for Red Sea shipping lanes.
IOM described the crisis sparked by the fighting as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the IOM last week.
More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, according to the IOM.
Fighting also broke out in Ethiopia last month in the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis renew warning over Saudi airports after deadly Riyadh attack
items.author: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.summary: The deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 at Riyadh's international airport.
items.body:
Yemen's Houthis warned airlines, travellers and airport workers on Sunday to stay away from Saudi airports, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"12 people"] and wounded more than 300 others.
It was the deadliest such attack in the kingdom in more than a decade and comes amid an escalation of [USN:S8N43806H TEXT:"fighting"] between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces.
"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theatre of operations for our forces, with the exception of the airports in (the holy cities of) Mecca and Medina," the Houthis said in a post on X.
"We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions."
Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said on Sunday that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.
"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television.
President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
The Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday that a projectile had also fallen near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The coalition also reported intercepting a drone in the region on Sunday.
INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD IN RIYADH Saturday's attack has forced the temporary closure of King Khalid International Airport but the Saudi energy ministry said a long-planned international energy conference was still going ahead in Riyadh on Sunday.
The five-day WPC Energy Congress is taking place at a convention centre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport. State TV said more than 70 ministers, 300 company executives and representatives of over 25 international energy organisations have confirmed their attendance.
It was not immediately clear whether the participants would attend in person or virtually.
A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum is also set to go ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available.
Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff.
In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the 12 dead included 4 Saudis, 2 Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said.
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said airport operations were temporarily suspended pending damage and safety assessments, without specifying when flights would resume.
Two previous attacks on Riyadh's international airport earlier in the week had killed four people and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.
items.raw_description: The deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 at Riyadh's international airport.

items.title: Smith sets new catching record as Australia take firm grip on test
items.author: Mark Gleeson
items.creator: Mark Gleeson
items.summary: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side took a firm grip on the first test with hosts South Africa 238 runs for eight wickets, still trailing the tourists by 152 runs at tea on the third day at Kingsmead.
items.body:
Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side took a firm grip on the first test with hosts South Africa 238 runs for eight wickets, still trailing the tourists by 152 runs at tea on the third day at Kingsmead.
Smith took three superb catches on Sunday to take his test tally to 222, going past the record of 220 held by England's Joe Root.
Two of the catches showed outstanding anticipation as Smith shuffled across a few steps to snag South Africa captain Temba Bavuma and Kyle Verreynne as they both tried reverse sweeps off the spin bowling of Nathan Lyon, and he also produced a flying dive across first slip to break the record and see off the threat of David Bedingham.
Australia captain Pat Cummins took 3-54 to lead a combined bowling effort as South Africa's batsmen were guilty of playing loose shots at crucial junctures of the contest with three wickets falling before lunch and four more in the second session.
South Africa added 57 runs to their overnight tally of 27-1 before Aiden Markram got a healthy edge as he tried to drive Mitch Starc and was caught by Matt Renshaw at first slip for 37.
An injudicious reverse sweep by Bavuma saw him go cheaply for three runs while Bedingham was out for 49, caught in spectacular fashion by Smith as he edged a back-foot drive.
After lunch, Cummins took two quick wickets with Wiaan Mulder (30) out to a miscued hook shot and Tristan Stubbs (32) following shortly as his pulled effort was caught at deep fine leg.
Marco Jansen and Verreynne went on the charge when they came to the wicket and both hit lusty blows, but a partnership of 35 runs from 34 balls was ended by Smith’s one-handed catch that saw Verreynne out for 13. Jansen (26 off 20 balls) perished three balls later, when he miscued the ball to be caught at mid-off with South Africa 197-8.
Simon Harmer (17 not out) and Keshav Maharaj (23 not out) were offering some late resistance for South Africa in an unbeaten 41-run partnership for the ninth wicket and will resume batting for the final session.
The opening two days of the test both ended early when bad light stopped play and extra time has been added on to all three of Sunday's sessions.

items.title: Los países de América Latina con las tarifas de electricidad residencial más altas y qué las encarece
items.author: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
items.summary: Dentro de la factura que pagan los hogares en la región también se tienen en cuenta la diferenciación de tarifas por franjas horarias, por estrato socioeconómico y, por su puesto, por niveles de consu ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — Los precios de la electricidad residencial en América Latina y el Caribe siguen presionando la inflación y podrían aumentar aún más por los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño y la guerra en Medio Oriente. La inflación energética anual se ubicó en 7,72% en julio en la región , por debajo del 8,03% registrado un mes antes. Sin embargo, el indicador todavía se mantiene por encima de la inflación total, que fue de 4,17% en julio en la región, según la Organización Latinoamericana y Caribeña de Energía (Olacde). Ver más: La inflación energética cede en América Latina en julio, pero aún supera a la general, según Olacde Según la última edición del Panorama Económico de América Latina y el Caribe del Grupo Banco Mundial , la volatilidad de los precios de la energía podría frenar el proceso desinflacionario y mantener una postura cautelosa de los bancos centrales. Esto prolongaría las elevadas tasas de interés reales, que restringen el crédito y la inversión. Asimismo, el Banco Mundial advirtió que El Niño podría afectar la agricultura y la generación hidroeléctrica, lo que podría provocar aumentos en los precios de los alimentos y la energía. En América Latina y el Caribe, el precio de la electricidad residencial depende principalmente de la matriz eléctrica y de los costos de generación, transmisión, distribución y comercialización. Según Olacde, la generación es el componente más importante, con cerca del 50% del total, seguida de la transmisión y distribución, que representan alrededor del 25%. “Uno de los principales factores que inciden en el precio de la electricidad para el usuario final es el costo de la generación eléctrica, el mismo que a la vez depende de la estructura de la matriz de generación”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea Andrés Rebolledo, secretario ejecutivo de Olacde. Si en dicha matriz tienen mayor participación fuentes primarias de costos nivelados bajos, como las energías renovables, el costo de generación también será bajo. Mientras que en una matriz de generación dependiente de combustibles o de tecnologías de alto costo de inversión y operación, el costo de la energía generada será también alto, anotó. Si la matriz de generación tiene alta dependencia de combustibles importados, el costo de generación será susceptible a la variación de los precios internacionales de dichos combustibles. Se estima que más del 60% de la electricidad generada en América Latina y el Caribe proviene de fuentes renovables. Ver más: Los dos países que impulsarán la producción petrolera de América Latina hasta 2050, según OPEP Los países más destacados son Paraguay (100%), Costa Rica (94%), Brasil (87%), Uruguay (87%), Venezuela (85%), Colombia (80%), Ecuador (78%) y Belice (75%). Según Olacde, los costos de transmisión y distribución también inciden en el costo de la electricidad a consumidor final. Sin embargo, por lo general estos suelen ser más estables que los costos de generación, pues dependen principalmente de la inversión y de los gastos fijos y variables de operación y mantenimiento de las redes de transmisión y distribución. Otros factores de peso son los cargos por pérdidas eléctricas y por potencia disponible. También pesan sobre la tarifa los impuestos, subsidios y aportes a fondos de compensación. Dentro de la factura que pagan los hogares en la región también se tienen en cuenta la diferenciación de tarifas por franjas horarias, por estrato socioeconómico y, por supuesto, por niveles de consumo. Olacde también menciona los cargos por servicios conexos como alumbrado público, cuerpo de bomberos, recolección de basura, entre otros. Según información de GlobalPetrolPrices, el precio promedio de la electricidad en el mundo fue de US$0,179 por kWh para usuarios residenciales y de US$0,172 por kWh para empresas hasta el tercer trimestre de 2026. “Los precios más altos de electricidad residencial se encuentran en Europa, con US$0,260 por kWh, y los más bajos en Asia, con US$0,088″, explica. Por su parte, África (US$0,141), Oceanía (US$0,253), Norteamérica (US$0,158) y Sudamérica (US$0,220) se encuentran en un punto intermedio. Fuente: GlobalPetrolPrices Con relación a sus pares, la gran ventaja comparativa de Paraguay se basa en el hecho de poseer, en condominio con dos países vecinos (Argentina y Brasil), dos grandes centrales hidroeléctricas que tienen un elevado factor de planta, aunque sus embalses sean relativamente pequeños, dijo a Bloomberg Línea el profesor Victorio Enrique Oxilia. “Esto significa que el país posee dos grandes centrales con elevada disponibilidad de energía firme”. El costo de generación depende, en buena medida, de la tarifa que la empresa eléctrica estatal Ande (Administración Nacional de Electricidad) debe pagar a las centrales binacionales Itaipú y Yacyretá. Itaipú, la principal fuente de energía de Paraguay, tiene una tarifa relativamente baja, de US$37 por MWh (megavatio-hora) de energía firme. Ver más: Así logró este país de América Latina generar toda su electricidad con fuentes 100% renovables Asimismo, ofrece condiciones de contratación favorables para la Ande, al menos hasta finales de 2026, explica Oxilia, profesor de la Facultad Politécnica de la Universidad Nacional de Asunción, en Paraguay. “La combinación actual de costos de generación de las tres centrales hidroeléctricas proveedoras del sistema eléctrico paraguayo se encuentra alrededor de 29 USD/MWh, uno de los costos más bajos del hemisferio.”, anotó el académico. “Esto permite que el costo de suministro sea relativamente bajo, aunque las pérdidas eléctricas sean elevadas (principalmente en distribución)”. Por otra parte, en los últimos tiempos, el hecho de vender a mineradoras de activos digitales en condiciones que elevan el factor de carga del sistema y con tarifas razonables también ha colaborado con el equilibrio financiero de la Ande. Sin embargo, “estas condiciones pueden cambiar a futuro: en el sentido positivo (se esperan tarifas más bajas de Itaipú), pero también en el sentido negativo (costos marginales elevados a futuro)”. La incidencia de El Niño en los costos de la electricidad para los consumidores en América Latina va a depender del impacto que el fenómeno tenga sobre todo en los sistemas de generación y transmisión. Este efecto varía según la ubicación de la infraestructura y su capacidad para resistir y adaptarse a las condiciones climáticas adversas. Ver más: El shock energético mundial persiste y obliga a los países a cambiar sus respuestas Por ejemplo, indicó Andrés Rebolledo, si los sistemas de generación se encuentran en zonas de incremento de precipitaciones y tienen un alto componente hidráulico, podrían verse beneficiados hasta cierto punto. Esto ocurriría siempre y cuando no se produzcan eventos extremos como inundaciones, que pongan en riesgo la integridad y operabilidad de las centrales hidráulicas. Un sistema eléctrico que depende principalmente de la generación hidroeléctrica puede verse afectado por las sequías, que reducen la disponibilidad de agua para producir energía. “En todo caso, los mercados más vulnerables ante el fenómeno de El Niño serían aquellos con una matriz de generación eléctrica con alta dependencia del recurso hidráulico”, indicó Rebolledo. En junio de 2026, la generación eléctrica de la región alcanzó los 163 TWh, lo que representó una contracción de 1,8% frente al mes anterior, según Olade. La hidroenergía aportó el 43,2% del total y se reafirmó como “la base estructural del suministro regional”, indicó el organismo. Olacde considera que los países de la región deberían fortalecer sus sistemas eléctricos para reducir la exposición de los consumidores a episodios de precios elevados de la energía. Para reducir la exposición, Olacde propone diversificar la matriz de generación eléctrica, con el fin de incrementar su resiliencia tanto ante eventos climáticos como ante coyunturas internacionales desfavorables. Asimismo, promover programas de uso racional y eficiente de la energía entre los consumidores. De otra parte, realizar una planificación eléctrica optimizada tanto desde el punto de vista energético como económico y ambiental, así como establecer mecanismos de compensación y estabilización de precios de la energía. También ve clave reducir al máximo las pérdidas de energía tanto en los procesos de generación como de transmisión y distribución de la electricidad. Si es necesario, desde Olacde proponen establecer subsidios focalizados para los sectores socioeconómicos más vulnerables. Ver más: Los tres países de Latinoamérica donde los precios se verían más impactados por El Niño 2026

items.title: Indonesia moves 8 endangered orangutans to safety after Borneo fires
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
items.body:
Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
The Southeast Asian nation is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, mainly on Sumatra and Borneo islands, and the government has warned the blazes could continue until November, aggravated by the El Niño weather pattern.
Three mother-child pairs and two adolescent male orangutans were among those rescued between August and September from several locations, the Indonesian government and wildlife foundation, Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) said in a statement.
"Their relocation to Batu Nyambu protected forest is expected to give the eight orangutans a chance to return to living naturally," the statement read.
Orangutans are critically endangered great apes found in the wild only on the Southeast Asian islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with Indonesia home to all three recognised species, according to the World Wildlife Fund. Populations have declined due to deforestation, wildfires and poaching.
The relocation operation took six hours by car, one hour on boats, and two more hours on foot, with the orangutans in cages carried on bamboo poles. Before they were moved, YIARI conservationists checked the animals' health.
Since August, the West Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency and YIARI have rescued 46 orangutans affected by fires, agency head Murlan Dameria Pane said.
From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since.
Haze from the fires has caused 175,000 cases of respiratory illness in Indonesia, with the smog affecting neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia where many schools were closed on Friday as air quality deteriorated.
items.raw_description: Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.

items.title: Kyiv propose à Moscou une désescalade réciproque sur l'énergie
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky s'est dit prêt dimanche à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cesse ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que le président américain Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses attaques.
items.body:
Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky s'est dit prêt dimanche à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cesse ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que le président américain Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses attaques.
Samedi, Donald Trump a imputé la hausse des prix du diesel aux États-Unis aux frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes et a déclaré que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement", ajoutant que l'Ukraine devrait le remplacer à sa tête car il avait laissé passer plusieurs occasions de conclure un accord avec Moscou.
La forte hausse des prix mondiaux du diesel, qui a suivi le déclenchement de la guerre avec l'Iran en février, est devenue un handicap politique pour le Parti républicain de Donald Trump à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat du mois prochain, lors desquelles les démocrates pourraient reprendre le contrôle d'une ou des deux chambres du Congrès.
Volodimir Zelensky a réaffirmé dimanche la position de longue date de l'Ukraine, selon laquelle elle est disposée à cesser ses attaques contre les raffineries russes uniquement dans le cadre d'une désescalade réciproque du conflit, qui exigerait que Moscou mette également fin à ses frappes contre les infrastructures électriques ukrainiennes.
Tout accord de ce type devrait s'accompagner de "garanties réelles", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky.
"La véritable cause de la guerre en Europe, c'est la Russie et la Russie seule", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky, sans faire directement référence aux propos de Donald Trump.
"Il est possible de mettre fin aux frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques dès aujourd'hui, mais Vladimir Poutine ne le veut pas."
Samedi, Volodimir Zelensky a réagi avec colère à l'annonce par Donald Trump d'un accord d'approvisionnement en diesel avec la Russie, estimant que celui-ci encouragerait les attaques de Moscou contre l'Ukraine.
Des analystes ont déclaré que l'accord conclu par Donald Trump avec Moscou avait peu de chances d'entraîner une baisse durable des prix des carburants, les volumes concernés restant bien inférieurs aux exportations habituelles de la Russie lorsque ses raffineries ne sont pas visées par des attaques.
L'accord sur le diesel a également été critiqué par des élus américains, dont le représentant républicain Don Bacon, qui a estimé qu'il était temps de renforcer les sanctions plutôt que de les alléger.
Dans les rues de Kyiv, plusieurs habitants ont fait part de leur colère après la suggestion de Donald Trump selon laquelle l'Ukraine devrait se trouver un nouveau dirigeant prêt à conclure un accord avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine.
"Personne n'a le droit de nous dire ce que nous devons faire, d'autant que des élections ne peuvent pas être organisées en temps de guerre", a déclaré Sabina, une institutrice de 40 ans, en référence à l'interdiction des élections en Ukraine sous le régime de la loi martiale pour des raisons de sécurité.
"À mes yeux, c'est une trahison de la part de nos partenaires", a-t-elle déclaré au sujet des remarques de Donald Trump.
Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré qu'il poursuivrait dimanche ses discussions avec les dirigeants européens et que des échanges avaient lieu quotidiennement sur des dispositifs supplémentaires de défense aérienne, notamment des munitions pour les avions de combat utilisés pour abattre les drones russes à réaction.
Lundi, le ministre ukrainien des Affaires étrangères, Andriï Sybiha, doit participer à une réunion du Conseil des affaires étrangères de l'Union européenne qui devrait examiner un renforcement de la pression des sanctions contre la Russie ainsi que l'avancement des négociations sur l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Union européenne.

items.title: Ukraine will stop hitting refineries if Russia halts energy attacks, Zelenskiy says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop its strikes.
items.body:
Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop its strikes.
On Saturday, Trump blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for raising US diesel prices and said Zelenskiy had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""], adding that Ukraine should replace him as leader because he had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow.
The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of next month's midterm elections, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress.
Zelenskiy on Sunday repeated Ukraine's long-standing position that it was willing to halt attacks on Russian refineries only as part of a mutual de-escalation of the conflict, which would require Moscow to cease its own strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure.
Any such deal would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said.
"The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said, without alluding specifically to Trump's remarks. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
On Saturday, Zelenskiy responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, which he said would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine.
Analysts said Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices, with the volumes still much lower than what Russia usually exports when its refineries are not under attack.
The diesel deal was also criticized by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions, not lift them.
On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher, referring to Ukraine's [USN:L1N44G089 TEXT:"prohibition on elections under martial law`"] for security reasons.
"In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks.
Zelenskiy said he would continue discussions with European leaders on Sunday, and there were daily conversations around additional air defence packages, including ammunition for combat aircraft that are used to down Russia's jet-powered drones.
On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is due to participate in a European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting that is expected to discuss increasing sanctions pressure on Russia and advancing negotiations on Ukraine’s EU accession.
items.raw_description: Ukraine is ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday, after US President Donald Trump demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop its strikes.

items.summary: Gea sends Shelton crashing out of Shanghai    Reuters
items.raw_description: Gea sends Shelton crashing out of Shanghai    Reuters

items.title: Gea sends Shelton crashing out of Shanghai
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday.
items.body:
US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday.
World number four Shelton, who has barely played since losing to Alexander Zverev in September's US Open final and withdrew from the Japan Open due to fitness concerns, lost both sets against the world number 56 in tight tiebreakers.
Asked if his recent lack of action had had an effect on him, Shelton told reporters: "I mean, I got outplayed today. The guy played better than me.
"A hundred percent, I would have liked to have come over here earlier and be prepared and have already dealt with the jet lag by the time I was playing here in the Shanghai Masters.
"My body wasn't ready. I wasn't physically ready to play in Tokyo. That's just the way this tour is sometimes."
The 24-year-old American said he was focused on finishing his 2026 campaign on a "high note" at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin next month.
"Obviously I want to be prepared and playing some of my best tennis when I get there," he added.
"Three tournaments left to finish the year, which has been a very up and down year, but a great year, on a high note."
Gea, who next faces either Jakub Mensik or Francisco Cerundolo, was delighted with his first win over a top-10 player.
"I'm practicing hard every day since the beginning of the year to win against those guys," he said.
"Of course, when you win, it is always special. But, yeah, I was prepared and I was confident before the match. Also playing a really good season right now, so, yeah, that's a really good win, but I was ready for it."

items.title: Nifty lags global peers as Korea, Taiwan markets surge on AI boom
items.author: Shilpa Rangarajan
items.summary: The Nifty 50 ranked second-last among 18 major markets over the past year, ahead only of Indonesia, Bloomberg data show ...
items.body: Indian equities have fallen behind their Asian and global peers, with the Nifty 50 ranking second-last ahead of only Indonesia among 18 major markets over the past year, Bloomberg data shows. The Nifty closed at 22,520.45 on Friday, down 10.6 per cent from a year earlier, days after touching an 18-month low. South Korea’s Kospi rose 86.7 per cent and Taiwan’s Taiex 80.6 per cent, leaving the Indian benchmark 97 and 91 percentage points behind. Only Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite, down 26.1 per cent, fared worse. The gap grew wider over two years, the data showed, as investors who put ₹100 in the Nifty in October 2024 now hold about ₹90. The same sum would be worth ₹255 in the Kospi, ₹218 in the Taiex, ₹176 in Japan’s Nikkei 225, ₹135 in the S&P 500, ₹128 in the London’s FTSE 100 and ₹117 in Hong Kong’s Hang Seng, in local-currency terms. The lag is not limited to Wall Street, where the S&P 500 rose 15.8 per cent in the past year and FTSE 100 10.9 per cent. The Nikkei gained 42.1 per cent and Singapore’s Straits Times 21.7 per cent. Even Hang Seng (down 9.5 per cent) and the Shanghai Composite (down 3.1 per cent) fell less than the Nifty.  South Korea and Taiwan rode a chipmaker rally on artificial-intelligence (AI) demand. Samsung Electronics returned 215 per cent including dividends, SK Hynix 352 per cent and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company 74.6 per cent. South Korea’s 10 largest companies together returned 211 per cent. G Chokkalingam of Equinomics Research doubts the chip-led rally will last. “My belief is that the AI boom is not sustainable,” he said, adding that he remains positive on India over the longer term. “So, I am very bullish. India will have an excellent future after 3-4 years. But before that, if this war continues for 6 months, we can have one big shock,” he said. India’s heavyweights went the other way. Its 10 most-valuable companies returned close to minus 20 per cent, dragged by Tata Consultancy Services (down 34.5 per cent), HDFC Bank (34 per cent), Hindustan Unilever (30 per cent) and Reliance Industries (21.6 per cent). Only about a third of Indian largecaps in the Bloomberg sample ended the year higher, against more than four in five in South Korea and Taiwan. The premium India long commanded over its neighbours has narrowed, but not because companies stopped making money. Aggregate profits of Indian firms in the sample rose about 6 per cent on Bloomberg’s prior-year comparison. Investors are simply paying less for them, and putting their money where the chips are.  “We missed a great opportunity to stand out. India does not figure in the top 10 destinations of global investors right now,” said Abhay Agarwal, founder and fund manager, Piper Serica. According to him, the private sector and innovation by large companies should be given more government support, along with more structured reforms, policies and regulations.  India’s large listed companies are now worth $3.67 trillion, less than Taiwan’s $4.59 trillion and barely ahead of Korea’s $3.62 trillion. In dollar terms, the Nifty 50’s market value has shrunk 17.3 per cent in a year to $1.88 trillion. A February 2 trade deal cut US tariffs on Indian goods to 18 per cent from 50 per cent, but the relief lasted less than four weeks. On February 28, the US and Israeli strikes on Iran triggered a war that has since choked shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. For a country that imports at least 88.7 per cent of its crude, the timing could hardly have been worse. Brent, at $72 before the war, topped $104 this week. Foreign investors pulled a record ₹1.14 trillion from Indian equities in March alone. The rupee has slid to about 96.7 to the dollar,  down 8.21 per cent over the past year and 7.09 per cent so far in 2026,  and on Wednesday the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 5.5 per cent, its first hike since February 2023. The currency has weakened 4.21 per cent over six months and 1.39 per cent over three months, while falling 5.95 per cent since the Iran war began. The rupee also fell 0.94 per cent in the current quarter and month, and 0.44 per cent over the past week. South Korea and Taiwan also import at least 94 per cent of their oil, but sustained massive gain due to their stakes in the semiconductor chip boom, which gave them an edge over Indian equities. Valuations have fallen with prices. The Nifty trades at 20.3 times earnings, down from 23.6 a year ago, implying its companies’ earnings rose about 4 per cent even as the index fell. The Taiex has risen to 27.9 times from 23.1. The Kospi’s multiple has dropped to 12.1 from 16.6 despite the rally, as profits outpaced prices. “The biggest worry for India is that the global oil price is up, and the rupee also depreciated. Hence, the impact has doubled. The rupee has to start recovering, and only then will the foreign institutional investor (FII) money come,” said Chokkalingam. “To get back the confidence of global investors, we need to get back on the high growth cycle which will require coordinated effort between the government and private sector,” Agarwal added.

items.title: Les Houthis renouvellent leurs menaces contre les aéroports saoudiens
items.author: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.summary: Les Houthis ont renouvelé dimanche leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, au lendemain d'une attaque contre l'aéroport international de Riyad qui a fait 12 morts, appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés.
items.body:
Les Houthis ont renouvelé dimanche leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, au lendemain d'une attaque contre l'aéroport international de Riyad qui a fait 12 morts, appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés.
Le groupe soutenu par l'Iran a déclaré que les aéroports et l'espace aérien saoudiens demeuraient des cibles potentielles d'opérations militaires et a averti que le royaume porterait la responsabilité de toute interception qui échouerait.
Ces nouvelles menaces interviennent alors que l'Arabie saoudite a maintenu l'accueil d'un important congrès international de l'énergie à Riyad.
Le ministère saoudien de l'Énergie a annoncé que le 25e Congrès mondial de l'énergie (WPC Energy Congress), d'une durée de cinq jours, a débuté dimanche, avec la participation confirmée de plus de 70 ministres, 300 dirigeants d'entreprises et représentants de plus de 25 organisations internationales du secteur de l'énergie, selon la télévision d'État.
La réunion ministérielle de l'International Energy Forum devait également se tenir dimanche, sa séance plénière étant organisée à huis clos, selon un avis aux médias.
L'attaque de samedi, la troisième visant l'aéroport de Riyad en une semaine, a fait au moins 12 morts et 309 blessés, selon les autorités saoudiennes. Parmi les victimes figurent quatre Saoudiens, deux Bangladais ainsi que des ressortissants des États-Unis, de Jordanie, de Palestine, de Syrie, du Soudan et d'Égypte.
L'autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile a déclaré que les opérations de l'aéroport avaient été temporairement suspendues dans l'attente d'évaluations des dégâts et des conditions de sécurité, sans préciser quand les vols reprendraient.
L'ambassade des États-Unis à Riyad a exhorté les citoyens américains à éviter l'aéroport et les zones environnantes. Elle a également précisé que les employés du gouvernement américain devaient obtenir une autorisation spéciale pour utiliser les aéroports de Riyad, Djeddah et Dammam.
Le président Donald Trump a déclaré samedi que Washington envisageait de se joindre aux frappes saoudiennes contre les Houthis et qu'une décision serait prise rapidement après cette attaque meurtrière.

items.title: INWIT shareholders explore financing for potential take-private deal
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone and KKR, are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT ...
items.body: The leading shareholders in INWIT are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers. French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone and KKR, are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT, the people said. Ardian controls 32% of INWIT, while Oak Holdings controls 39%. The investors are discussing the financing of the bid with banks, the people said, with one person adding that Abu Dhabi investment firm Mubadala is expected to take a stake in INWIT as part of the plan. The people cautioned that deliberations are still ongoing. Ardian, GIP, Vodafone, KKR and Mubadala declined to comment. GIP is part of US investment firm Blackrock . An INWIT spokesperson said the company did not have any information on the matter. INWIT, which listed in Milan in 2015, has been the subject of takeover speculation since a French media report in February that infrastructure fund Ardian and investment group Brookfield were interested in taking the Italian company private. INWIT has since then become embroiled in a dispute with its two main customers, Telecom Italia (TIM) and Swisscom's Fastweb, both of which have initiated procedures to terminate their respective contracts with INWIT as part of efforts to renegotiate them on more favourable terms. INWIT's market value has fallen about 27% over the past year to $7.1 billion (€6.3 billion) as of Friday's close, according to LSEG data.

items.title: INWIT investors line up financing for possible take-private, sources say
items.author: Elvira Pollina, Amy-Jo Crowley, Valentina Za
items.creator: Elvira Pollina, Amy-Jo Crowley, Valentina Za
items.summary: The leading shareholders in INWIT are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers.
items.body:
The leading shareholders in INWIT (INWT.MI) are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers.
French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone (VOD.L) and KKR (KKR.N) , are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT, the people said.
Ardian controls 32% of INWIT, while Oak Holdings controls 39%.
The investors are discussing the financing of the bid with banks, the people said, with one person adding that Abu Dhabi investment firm Mubadala is expected to take a stake in INWIT as part of the plan.
The people cautioned that deliberations are still ongoing.
Ardian, GIP, Vodafone (VOD.L) , KKR (KKR.N) and Mubadala declined to comment. GIP is part of US investment firm Blackrock (BLK.N) .
An INWIT spokesperson said the company did not have any information on the matter.
INWIT, which listed in Milan in 2015, has been the subject of [USN:L6N40C0Y4 TEXT:"takeover speculation"] since a French media report in February that infrastructure fund Ardian and investment group Brookfield were interested in taking the Italian company private.
INWIT has since then become [USN:L8N43G1LQ TEXT:"embroiled in a dispute"] with its two main customers, Telecom Italia (TIM) (TLIT.MI) and Swisscom's Fastweb (SCMN.S) , both of which have initiated procedures to terminate their respective contracts with INWIT as part of efforts to renegotiate them on more favourable terms.
INWIT's market value has fallen about 27% over the past year to $7.1 billion (€6.3 billion) as of Friday's close, according to LSEG data.
(1 euro = $1.1201)
