items.title: Polish security services meet after 'serious' threat to PM and defence minister
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.
items.body:
Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said.
Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not go into details but authorities were treating the threat as "deadly serious".
"We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out," he told reporters.
Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security.
While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.
In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of [USN:L1N44I06W TEXT:"calling for the assassination"] of senior Polish politicians.
In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an [USN:L1N3W206N TEXT:"assassination attempt"] on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

items.title: From theatre to streets, Gen Z protester Neha Bora a new face of India's youth unrest
items.author: Aftab Ahmed, Saurabh Sharma
items.creator: Aftab Ahmed, Saurabh Sharma
items.summary: The 29-year-old doctoral student said she did not set out to become an activist.
items.body:
A little-known doctoral student has emerged as one of the most visible faces of a protest movement in India that has mounted the most serious challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government in years.
Neha Bora, 29, is one of a number of prominent activists detained this weekend as the authorities cracked down on attempts by protesters led by the "Cockroach" youth movement to demonstrate against what they say is massive vote-rigging to help Modi's party.
But Bora, national president of the left-wing All India Students’ Association, says she did not set out to become an activist. She traces her path into politics to theatre and, later, the student-led protests against a citizenship law in 2019 and 2020.
BORA URGES PROTESTERS ON FROM DETENTION On Saturday, after police blocked demonstrators from reaching New Delhi's designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, Bora urged them to regroup at Dilli Haat, a crafts market 10 km (6 miles) away.
"Dilli Haat becomes Jantar Mantar today," she wrote on X before setting off towards the site, chanting slogans as others followed.
Police detained her with several other activists. But even in detention, she called for the demonstration to continue.
"I am in detention. The movement is not," she said in a video posted online, urging supporters who were stopped by police to protest wherever they were. She was released later on Saturday.
The Cockroach Janta Party-led protests seek the ouster of India's election chief, claiming irregularities in handling voter data have led to the deletion of 130 million names — more than the population of Japan — from electoral rolls.
The Election Commission denies favouring any group, and Modi's Hindu nationalist party has accused opponents of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Other issues Bora has championed include school-examination scandals, unemployment and police actions.
Soft-spoken in conversation but forceful behind a microphone, she has built a following through speeches in Hindi and English, often invoking constitutional rights and linking student grievances to broader questions of inequality and government accountability.
'HOPE IS ALSO INFECTIOUS' Bora grew up in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand and moved frequently as a child because her father served in the army. She studied at Delhi University before beginning a doctorate at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics.
As an undergraduate, she told Reuters in an interview this month, she joined a theatre group, where she learned to inhabit the lives of people much different from herself.
"There might be a character that if you meet in your real life, you will disagree with, you will not like. But to do theatre is to understand where that person comes from."
A turning point was the citizenship law, which critics say discriminates against Muslims.
Bora said she watched students of her own generation lead classmates out of lecture halls and onto the streets, turning ideas she had encountered in books, films and documentaries into political action.
She gained wider attention during protests in July over alleged leaks of exam papers, when she joined other activists in demanding the resignation of the education minister. Her speeches at Jantar Mantar, criticising the government and police response to demonstrators, circulated widely online.
Bora has since become a fixture at demonstrations in the capital. During protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, she was repeatedly detained and returned to the streets after her release.
She said ideology alone does not drive the current mobilisation, describing hope as a more powerful force.
"Fear is infectious, of course. But hope is also infectious," she said. "People have courage now because they think that they can have courage."
Bora said the demonstrations reflect the accumulation of years of grievances.
"People remember," she said. "People carry that discontent, people carry that betrayal, people carry that disappointment."
items.raw_description: The 29-year-old doctoral student said she did not set out to become an activist.

items.title: Imran Khan's provincial government suspended by Pakistan president over militancy fight
items.author: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
items.creator: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
items.summary: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.
items.body:
Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, the president's office said, following allegations it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.
The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.
The provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months.
The move comes after Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party rallied for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to [USN:L8N45R072 TEXT:"march on the capital"] Islamabad in coming days amid deepening political instability.
The federal government and the military have accused Khan's party of failing to curb Islamist militants in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, which has suffered an increasing number of [USN:L1N43Z03Y TEXT:"militant attacks"] in recent months.
Khan's party rejects the allegation, saying the federal government failed to provide the provincial government with funding and equipment to combat the militancy.
"The situation is so grave that you wouldn't see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.
Islamabad accuses neighbouring Afghanistan of harboring Islamist militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says that Khan's party had been sympathizing with both the Taliban in Kabul and their affiliates at home.
Both the Afghan Taliban and Khan's party have denied the accusation.
President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif following a federal cabinet decision, the president's office said.
"This is more of a coup disguised as emergency," said Zulfikar Bukhari, Khan's aide and his party's spokesperson.
Bukhari said it was a "ridiculous decision" that would only lead to further bloodshed and instability.
The country's powerful military is widely seen as the ultimate power broker to decide who will rule the South Asian nation of 240 million. Khan's supporters say the military rigged the 2024 election against the 74-year-old former cricket star, an allegation the military denies.
KHAN'S PARTY CHIEF MINISTER'S MOVEMENT BLOCKED Ahead of the planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists in recent days.
Restrictions have been placed on Chief Minister, Sohail Afridi of Khan's party in the northwestern province, one of his close aides told Reuters. All roads leading to his office had been blocked with shipping containers, with hundreds of police deployed, said witnesses.
The PTI's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.
The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said.
STANDOFF OVER KHAN'S HEALTH The standoff comes more than a month after the government defied a court order and refused to allow Khan's treatment in a private hospital, despite mounting concerns over [USN:FWN44F00T TEXT:"his health"].
The protest also coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.
Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. He says he is a political prisoner and the military is making up charges to keep him out of the country's politics, a charge the army denies.
Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violent attacks on military and state installations, and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.
All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.

items.title: Bezzecchi pips Fernandez to win Indonesian GP, Martin retakes championship lead
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez.
items.body:
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez.
[USN:L4N45W00O TEXT:"Polesitter Fernandez"], racing with fractured fingers sustained in a crash on Saturday, looked untroubled in the opening half of the race as he and Bezzecchi surged away from the chasing pack.
But the Trackhouse rider began to fade as the afternoon wore on, and a determined Bezzecchi finally pounced with nine laps remaining to seize the lead and secure victory, with Martin completing a podium lockout for Italian manufacturer Aprilia.
Bezzecchi's win, the 300th victory for an Italian in MotoGP, also kept his faint championship hopes alive.
"I'm very, very happy to be back on the top step of the podium," said the 27-year-old, who led the standings in the early stages of the season but has struggled in recent weeks.
"It was a nice, nice battle with Raul. I think we deserve a result like this, me and all my team, especially them, because they never stop working. They've been through tough times with me."
A dejected Fernandez revealed the full extent of his injury after the race.
"Yesterday, when I crashed and I saw my hand, I knew before going to the clinic that I had my finger broken, the one that normally I used to brake," the Spaniard said.
"This morning, when I woke up, I realised I don't have one, but two fingers broken. No one knew. I tried to say nothing, just keep the pain for me and keep my focus on the race.
"This morning, I tried find a solution on the brakes, because I was not able to use the finger that I use normally. I started everything from zero. It was a very difficult job for me."
MARTIN BACK AT THE TOP The most exciting duel in the race took place behind the top three, with Marquez engaging in a thrilling back-and-forth with KTM's Pedro Acosta.
Marquez had a strong start and swooped into third place in the opening lap, but his Ducati struggled to keep pace with the Aprilia machines around him, and a hard-charging Martin picked him off with ease in the third lap.
The defending champion was then quickly overtaken by Acosta, but for the second time in as many days, Marquez profited from tyre pressure issues for his opponent and was allowed back into fourth.
When Acosta was sure he would not receive a penalty, he once again locked horns with Marquez, but as they traded blows, Trackhouse's Ai Ogura capitalised and moved past both riders to seal a first-ever 1-2-3-4 finish for Aprilia.
Martin, the 2024 champion, moved up to 355 points at the top of the championship standings, with [USN:L1N45W01V TEXT:"Saturday's sprint-winner Marquez"] on 353 points after finishing in sixth place - the first time he has completed a full race at the Mandalika circuit.
"The last few laps, I was struggling a lot with the tyres, physical condition, but I was able to finish on the podium, so really, really happy," Martin said.
"We are still in the fight. We are still in the lead. It will be a tough championship, but I will give my all."

items.title: Hurricanes aim to extend win streak to 5, add to Flyers' woes
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions.
items.body:
Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions.
The Hurricanes aim for their fifth straight victory Sunday when they visit the winless Flyers for the second consecutive weekend.
Carolina lost its first two games before posting a 3-2 triumph in Philadelphia on Oct. 3. Former Flyer Shayne Gostisbehere scored the overtime winner for the Hurricanes, who used that victory as a springboard to three more wins.
Most recently, Carolina posted a 5-2 road victory over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday. Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook each registered a goal and an assist for the Hurricanes.
"Every single line is contributing," Martinook said. "The 'D' is playing some of the best hockey I've ever seen the group play together. ... It's been fun to watch."
Sebastian Aho added a shorthanded goal for his team-leading fifth goal, while Mark Jankowski and Taylor Hall also scored for the defending Stanley Cup champions.
"We've definitely, after the first couple games, gotten into our game," Aho said. "Just playing Hurricanes hockey, and that usually gives you a chance to win."
The Hurricanes have scored 21 goals during their four-game winning streak. Jankowski has scored in each of the last three games, while Brandon Bussi has earned the victory in each of his last two starts.
"It was a good effort from pretty much everyone," Carolina coach Rod Brind'Amour said. "I liked it. ... When we're going, you can tell we're in sync."
Philadelphia, meanwhile, has lost 10 straight games dating back to its second-round playoff series against Carolina. The Hurricanes swept the Flyers last spring en route to winning the Stanley Cup, and the hangover has continued into the current campaign, as Philadelphia is 0-4-2.
"It's not like we're not trying," said rookie forward Porter Martone, who scored the Flyers' goal in Saturday's 5-1 road loss to the Boston Bruins. "These guys in this group, we care. I think a lot of people from the outside think it's lack of effort, but everyone in this room is giving it their all. We don't like this. We're not having fun right now. We want to win."
Philadelphia has been outshot by a wide margin and outscored 24-7 in its first six games. The Flyers scored only three goals while going 0-2-1 on their three-game road trip that ended Saturday.
The last time the Flyers lost their first six games was in 2008-09, when the team began 0-3-3 before rallying to make the postseason.
"You've got to stick together," said Philadelphia coach Rick Tocchet, whose team played Saturday without forward Travis Konecny and defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York. "We're at the bottom. We're in the muck right now. Hopefully, we get some healthy bodies back, but you've just got to stick together. There's no other answer. We've all been, in life, in a situation where you're in a foxhole and we need some people to sit in a foxhole and stick together."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Saudi stocks slide after attack on Riyadh airport
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Saudi stocks fell on Sunday, a day after an attack on Riyadh's international airport killed at least 12 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
items.body:
Saudi stocks fell on Sunday, a day after an [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attack on Riyadh's international airport"] killed at least 12 people and wounded over 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) dropped 1% with most of its constituents in negative territory, including top lender Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) , which was down 1%. Oil major Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) was down 0.6%.
Despite missile attacks on Riyadh's airport this week, organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"will go ahead"] this month.
President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis, widening a regional conflict that spilled over from the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Riyadh, along with the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes against targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
In Qatar, the index (.QSI) retreated 1%, with petrochemical maker Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA) declining 2.2%.

items.title: Rangers begin life without Igor Shesterkin vs. slumping Canucks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night.
items.body:
The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night.
On Saturday, the Rangers found out Shesterkin's season was over, and his absence threatens to derail a promising start for a team coming off missing the playoffs for the past two seasons.
Dylan Garand will step in as the 2021-22 Vezina Trophy winner's replacement for the time being, and the Rangers hope his promise in limited action translates to success in regular work starting Sunday night when they host the Vancouver Canucks.
Shesterkin, 30, was injured when his right skate collided with the goal post while sliding into position to make a save with 11:40 remaining in the second period of Friday's 3-1 loss at Washington, which halted a four-game winning streak.
Shesterkin's season is over after he was 3-1-0 with a 1.79 goals-against average. The Rangers are now counting on Garand, who is 3-1-1 with a 1.31 GAA in five career games.
"You never want to see guys get injured, especially your best player in Igor," Garand, 24, told reporters at practice Saturday. "He means a lot to the guys in this room and a lot to me personally. ... I'm excited for the opportunity. Going to put my heart and soul on the line for these guys and this city every night and just try to help the team win."
Garand began this season third on New York's depth chart and was exposed to waivers before getting claimed. He is being elevated because Joonas Korpisalo is out for at least four more weeks due to a lower-body injury. Garand's backup will be journeyman Spencer Martin, who made six appearances last season when Shesterkin was injured in January and went 1-3-0 with a 4.13 GAA.
"A guy (Shesterkin) that means so much to our team," defenseman Adam Fox told reporters at practice Saturday. "Obviously, still processing that and you still feel terrible. Personally having dealt with injuries the past few years and him, too, it (stinks) when you're not able to be out there and help the team. He's such an important piece to this team. It's an opportunity for everyone else to step up."
The Rangers are hoping Garand can help them open a season 4-0 at home for the first time since 2009-10 after outscoring Tampa Bay, Utah and the Islanders 14-5.
Vancouver has allowed a league-leading 29 goals through its first six games, including 14 in a three-game skid against the Vegas Golden Knights, Carolina Hurricanes and New Jersey Devils. The Canucks have permitted 98 shots on goal in their past three games, and have allowed three power-play goals apiece in the past two games.
"From a work ethic standpoint, it just needs to be much more difficult for teams to recover pucks and get to their sets," first-year coach Manny Malhotra said of Vancouver's penalty-killing woes.
Last season, the Canucks had the NHL's worst penalty-kill percentage at 71.5%.
"That's a couple games in a row where our penalty kill has to bear down and get those kills," Vancouver forward Brock Boeser said after taking a pair of penalties against the Devils. "We got to stay out of the box, myself included."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Russia's Yandex says data centre in Vladimir area shut down after drone attack
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Sunday that its infrastructure had been damaged in a drone attack, resulting in the complete shutdown of its data centre in the Vladimir region.
items.body:
Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Sunday that its infrastructure had been damaged in a drone attack, resulting in the complete shutdown of its data centre in the Vladimir region.
No one was injured in the attack, but some of Yandex's services are currently unavailable to users, the company said.
This is the third major data centre to have been taken out of action in the last few days.
On Friday, Yandex, which is heavily involved in Russia's AI development and is sometimes called "Russia's Google", [USN:R4N45F01R TEXT:"said"] its data centre in the Kaluga region southwest of Moscow had been struck by Ukrainian drones and partly put out of action.
A day earlier, a Ukrainian attack [USN:L1N45U04H TEXT:"shut down"] Yandex's data hub in Sasovo, southeast of Moscow, where two of the three supercomputers used to develop the company's AI model are housed.

items.title: FII selloff intensifies! Foreign investors sell Indian equities worth Rs 45,000 crore in just 6 sessions
items.author: Debaroti Adhikary
items.summary: Foreign investors sold Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in October's first six sessions, nearly matching September's outflows. Elevated US bond yields and crude oil prices continue to pressure markets, while inflation data and geopolitical developments could influence the selling trend.
items.body: FII selloff has intensified in October, with foreign investors net selling Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in just six sessions in October so far, nearly the same as the total Rs 45,536 crore outflows recorded in the entire month of September. Analysts have listed factors that could change the trend and ease pressure on the market.The Indian stock market snapped a record eight-week-long losing streak last week, ending with gains despite strong upswings and downswings. Yet, FIIs remained bearish and continued selling Indian equities in every session so far in October. The foreign investors have remained net sellers of Indian equities for 11 consecutive sessions since mid-September.What's behind the massive FII outflows?The sharp FII selloff came as bond yields soared to multi-year highs, making the risk-free returns from the debt market more lucrative than equities. The 10-year US Treasury yield recorded its biggest quarterly increase of the 21st century in the three months ended September, Reuters reported. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries climbed above 5.3%, surpassing its 2007 peak and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that the rapid acceleration in FII outflows in October so far has taken the total FPI equity selling in 2026 to a whopping Rs 3,60,952 crore. “This massive FPI selling is the primary reason why the Indian market is underperforming this year with negative 13.87% Nifty returns so far in 2026,” he said.Also read | D-St Exit Rush! Sectors that saw sharpest FII selloff in 2nd half of SeptemberWhen can the trend reverse?From the FPI perspective, the rationale behind the massive outflows is the risk-free return from the 10-year US bonds being above 5.2%, according to the analyst. “So long as the US bond yields remain elevated, FPIs will continue to sell. The scenario will change when the valuations become attractive, and the risk-reward ratio turns favourable for investment,” Vijayakumar explained.Over the last two months, the market has been steadily trending down. Elevated crude prices and high US bond yields are the two headwinds for the market now, he added, warning that so long as these headwinds remain strong, the market will remain under pressure.Going ahead, investors will closely track US and Indian inflation data, US bond yields, Brent crude prices and developments in US-Iran geopolitical tensions in the coming week, according to Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President of Research at Bajaj Broking.Also read | FIIs dump Indian stocks for eight straight weeks: Is a reversal on the cards or more pain ahead?Technical view on NiftyGoing forward, the 22,350–22,330 zone could act as immediate support for Nifty, according to Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities. He noted that a decisive move below this zone could trigger renewed selling pressure towards 22,200.On the upside, the 22,660–22,680 zone, coinciding with the 10-day EMA, could act as an immediate hurdle, according to the analyst, who feels that a sustained move above this zone could trigger short covering and extend the pullback towards 22,820. Despite the recent recovery, confirmation through sustained buying remains necessary, he warned.Also read | Nifty bulls regain momentum, but can bears strike back? 5 factors to decide D-Street’s fate next weekDisclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.author: Munsif Vengattil
items.creator: Munsif Vengattil
items.summary: Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO.
items.body:
Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO.
Jio Platforms, which owns the telecom arm, is targeting a [USN:L4N45V0VX TEXT:"valuation of $106 billion"] in the offering. Much like SpaceX-owned (SPCX.O) Starlink, Jio's own satellite venture is also awaiting final security clearance to launch.
Cheap data is the playbook that built Jio in India, and the one Musk has used in markets [USN:L1N3KA0IB TEXT:"like Kenya"] to unsettle local telecom players. SpaceX now plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, [USN:L4N45V0TK TEXT:"starting in the US"].
Musk did not specify prices for India, where mobile data costs about 8 cents per gigabyte, among the lowest in the world.
"Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable," he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday.
"The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," Musk added.
'PRIME MINISTER AMBANI' The billionaire's remarks were the latest in a [USN:L4N45V0R8 TEXT:"series of X posts"] where he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's entry into one of the world's biggest internet markets to favour market leader Jio.
The posts have marked a sharp turn for Musk, who has long enjoyed a warm public rapport with Modi.
India's government has denied any bias in its approval process, noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink's and Jio's, are all awaiting final security clearance.
Late on Friday, Musk taunted Ambani directly, addressing him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would "consider allowing Starlink to compete".
Reliance has not responded to requests for comment on Musk's remarks.

items.title: インド、選管トップ辞任要求で厳戒続く　「ゴキブリ党」創設者ら釈放
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] - インドの首都ニューデリーは１１日、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める若者らの抗議活動が２日目を迎えるのを前に警戒が続いている。裁判所は、警察が前日拘束した若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」創設者アビジート・ディプケ氏ら幹部３人の釈放を命じた。

ニューデリーでは１０日、有権者名簿の見直しを巡り、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める数千人規模の抗議集会が予定されていた。当局は集会を阻止するため市中心部を封鎖。ディプケ氏らはデリーに到着した航空機から降りる際に拘束された。

ＣＪＰの法務責任者ラトナ・シン氏は、ディプケ氏らが今後１年間、治安を乱さないことを条件に釈放されたとＸに投稿した。ソーシャルメディアで著名な活動家ドルーブ・ラティ氏も拘束されていたが、内務省当局者によると、今後の抗議活動に参加しないことを条件に１１日未明に釈放された。

警察は１０日、２０００人以上を拘束。１１日も数千人の警察官や準軍事組織要員を市内各地に配置した。１０日に拘束された人の大半は同日夜までに釈放された。

野党やモディ政権の批判勢力は、抗議参加者に対する当局の対応は強権的だと批判。国連機関も平和的な集会の権利を保障するようインド当局に求めた。

インド外務省は１１日、国連の対応を批判し、声明は「インドの内政への不当な干渉だ」と反発した。

抗議活動では、有権者名簿の見直しがモディ首相の与党インド人民党（ＢＪＰ）に不当に有利に働いているとして、ギャネシュ・クマール選挙管理委員長の辞任を求めている。選管とＢＪＰはこうした指摘を否定している。

items.author: CNA
items.summary: Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.

Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief

Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.

Security personnel are seen at a blocked road amid ongoing protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Sajjad Hussain)

FAST

NEW DELHI: New Delhi braced for a second day of youth protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief on Sunday (Oct 11), as a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) , and the other leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
They were produced in front of a magistrate early on Sunday.
"Condition - no breach of peace for one year," the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said in a post on X announcing their release.

Activist and social media influencer Dhruv Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.

Related:

Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder ahead of youth protest

India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest

Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said.
Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.
India's foreign ministry said on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."

A man rides a scooter past shuttered shops in a deserted market, on the second day of a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Bhawika Chhabra)

MILLIONS OF NAMES REMOVED FROM ELECTORAL ROLL The protests are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Commuters cross a checkpoint as police officers stand guard on the second day of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Priyanshu Singh)

Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
The cockroach party, which began as an online satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister.
The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles, and said it would not stop until India's election system was reformed.

Activist and social media influencer Dhruv Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.

Related:

Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder ahead of youth protest

India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest

Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said.
Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.
India's foreign ministry said on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."

A man rides a scooter past shuttered shops in a deserted market, on the second day of a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Bhawika Chhabra)

MILLIONS OF NAMES REMOVED FROM ELECTORAL ROLL The protests are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Commuters cross a checkpoint as police officers stand guard on the second day of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Priyanshu Singh)

Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
The cockroach party, which began as an online satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister.
The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles, and said it would not stop until India's election system was reformed.

items.title: NHL roundup: Mitch Marner's OT goal vs. Kings keeps Knights rolling
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
items.body:
Mitch Marner scored a 4-on-3 power-play goal at 2:40 of overtime to give the Vegas Golden Knights a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
With Scott Laughton in the penalty box for tripping Shea Theodore six seconds earlier, Marner snapped a wrist shot from the high slot past a screen by Mark Stone and beyond the glove of Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper for the game-winner and his second goal of the season. It was Marner's eighth career overtime winner and his first with the Golden Knights.
Trevor Connelly scored a goal and assisted on the game-winner, while Stone had two assists for Vegas, which extended its winning streak to four games. Carter Hart made 26 saves for the Golden Knights, who leapfrogged the Edmonton Oilers to move back into first place in the Pacific Division.
Artemi Panarin scored the lone goal for Los Angeles, which remains winless (0-2-2) under first-year head coach Peter Laviolette. The Kings also have opened a season with four consecutive losses for the first time in franchise history.
Maple Leafs 6, Avalanche 3
William Nylander had two goals and three assists, Auston Matthews had two goals and two assists, and Toronto downed Colorado in Denver.
Nylander's three assists and five points matched his career highs. Easton Cowan and Nick Blankenburg also scored, Nick Paul had two assists and Sergei Bobrovsky turned away 30 shots for the Maple Leafs.
Nathan MacKinnon had two goals, Brock Nelson also scored and Mackenzie Blackwood had 17 saves for the Avalanche, who lost for the first time in three home games this season.
Wild 4, Panthers 1
Kirill Kaprizov tallied his seventh career hat trick and added an assist, and Minnesota handed host Florida its first regulation loss of the season in Sunrise, Fla.
Matt Boldy had the other Wild goal, on a wrist shot 53 seconds into the game. He also assisted on one of Kaprizov's tallies. Goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 of 30 shots to earn the victory as Minnesota ended a two-game winless skid.
Matthew Tkachuk scored Florida's lone goal, off a rebound of his own shot in the second period. Goaltender Jacob Markstrom allowed three goals on 28 shots.
Lightning 5, Islanders 3
Brandon Hagel ripped a tiebreaking goal with 1:44 remaining and completed his fourth career hat trick with an empty-netter as Tampa Bay claimed its fourth straight victory, beating host New York.
Tied 3-all, Hagel rifled a shot past Ilya Sorokin (21 saves) with a long wrister for his second goal. He added an assist for a four-point night. Jake Guentzel tallied twice, and Nikita Kucherov and Max Crozier each had two assists. Goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots.
Tony DeAngelo recorded a goal and an assist, and Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Brayden Schenn scored as the Islanders lost for the first time in three games on home ice.
Bruins 5, Flyers 1
Capping a three-point effort, Fraser Minten's second goal of the season concluded a three-goal third period for Boston in a win over visiting Philadelphia.
Pavel Zacha and Mason Lohrei scored to give Boston leads after the first two periods. Marat Khusnutdinov and Casey Mittelstadt also lit the lamp, while Minten and JJ Peterka each had two assists and Jeremy Swayman made 14 saves.
Porter Martone scored a power-play goal and Dan Vladar (27 saves) took the loss for Philadelphia, which remains winless in six games this season. The Flyers were missing Travis Konecny (lower-body) and Cam York (upper-body) due to day-to-day injuries.
Oilers 3, Sharks 1
Tristan Jarry made 19 saves as Edmonton skated to a win against host San Jose.
Mattias Ekholm, Vasily Podkolzin and Alex Formenton scored while Connor McDavid increased his early-season points total to 13 with an assist for the Oilers, who have won four straight games since dropping their season opener to the Vancouver Canucks.
Macklin Celebrini's first goal of the season was the lone score for the Sharks, who have dropped two of their last three. Celebrini, who missed two games with a lower-body injury, led San Jose with 21:59 of ice time and placed two shots on goal. Yaroslav Askarov made 17 saves.
Canadiens 1, Red Wings 0
Zack Bolduc scored the only goal of a shootout that went three extra rounds to give host Montreal the win over Detroit.
Because the game was scoreless after 65 minutes both goalies -- Jacob Fowler of Montreal and Detroit's Daniil Tarasov -- were credited with a shutout. Both made 30 saves and both picked up their second career shutout.
There were chants from the Montreal crowd of "We want Larkin" at times when the Red Wings' Dylan Larkin was on the ice, but booed him during his shootout attempt. Larkin asked to be traded in the.
Hurricanes 5, Blackhawks 2
Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook both scored once and added an assist, and visiting Carolina used a three-goal second period to beat slumping Chicago.
Mark Jankowski, Sebastian Aho and Taylor Hall also scored for the Hurricanes, who have won four straight games. Goaltender Brandon Bussi made 24 saves and Mike Reilly collected two assists.
Roman Kantserov, with his first NHL goal, and Oliver Moore replied for the Blackhawks, while goalie Spencer Knight made 34 saves. Chicago has just one win in six games to start the season.
Mammoth 4, Sabres 1
Utah scored twice on its league-leading power play and routed host Buffalo.
After Buffalo's Tage Thompson and Utah's Kailer Yamamoto traded goals in the first period, the Mammoth broke the game open with two goals in just over two minutes late in the middle frame.
Karel Vejmelka made 23 saves in his third win of the season while Colten Ellis stopped 26 in the loss. Yamamoto, John Marino and offseason acquisition Anders Lee each recorded a goal and an assist in the win.
Devils 4, Canucks 1
Nico Hischier scored twice on the power play, including his 200th career goal, and New Jersey rallied to beat Vancouver in Newark, N.J.
Jake Allen made 20 saves in his 500th career game to get the win as the Devils snapped a two-game losing skid. Jesper Bratt had a goal and an assist, Jesper Boqvist also scored and Jack Hughes had two assists for the Devils, who finished with three goals on the power play to claim their second win of the season.
Linus Karlsson had a goal while Leevi Merilainen and Kevin Lankinen combined to stop 33 shots for the Canucks, who suffered their third consecutive loss. Paul Cotter, the NHL's Third Star of the Week, was held pointless in his first game with the Canucks against his former team.
Senators 3, Predators 2 (SO)
Shane Pinto beat Matt Murray in the third round of the shootout as Ottawa rallied for a win over visiting Nashville.
Tim Stutzle had a goal and an assist in regulation and scored in the second round of the shootout. Drake Batherson also scored for the Senators, while Ottawa goaltender Linus Ullmark stopped 16 shots.
Ross Colton and Jonathan Marchessault scored first-period goals, and Ryan O'Reilly had a shootout goal for Nashville. Murray recorded 18 saves in his first start since the 2023-24 season, when he played for the Dallas Stars.
Penguins 2, Stars 1 (SO)
Rickard Rakell scored the shootout winner in the fourth round and host Pittsburgh edged Dallas. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby also tallied in the shootout for the Penguins while Seguin and Wyatt Johnston scored for the Stars.
After Rakell's goal put Pittsburgh up, goalie Arturs Silovs deflected Mikko Rantanen's shot to end it.
The Stars forced overtime when Tyler Seguin tied it 1-1 with 30 seconds left in regulation. Jake Oettinger made 19 saves. Connor Dewar scored his first goal of the season for the Penguins. Silovs made 24 saves to earn the victory.
Blues 5, Blue Jackets 3
Jimmy Snuggerud scored two second-period goals in quick succession and Jonatan Berggren scored the game-winning goal to help St. Louis halt its three-game slide with a home win over Columbus.
The Blues entered the matchup buried in offensive woes during their three-game losing skid but found their flow as Jake Neighbours and Pavel Buchnevich also found the back of the net and Dylan Holloway picked up three assists. Jordan Binnington made 20 saves as he recorded his first victory of the season.
Cole Sillinger, Kent Johnson, and Valeri Nichushkin lit the lamp for the Blue Jackets, while Jet Greaves finished with 22 saves.
Ducks 4, Flames 2
Ryan Poehling broke a third-period tie and added an assist to pace visiting past winless Calgary.
Frank Vatrano, Jackson LaCombe and Nikita Nesterenko also scored, and Mikael Granlund had two assists for the Ducks, who have won four of their first five games. Goaltender Ville Husso made 27 saves in his first start of the season for the win.
Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev each scored, and Matt Coronato collected two assists for the Flames, who have lost their first five games in the worst start in franchise history and are the only without a point this season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: World Bank in talks with dozens of countries about crisis aid, Banga says
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview.
items.body:
The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview.
Banga said the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial [USN:S0N3XA08Z TEXT:"$25 billion in crisis funds"] that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February.
However, a sharp spike in diesel and fertilizer prices and other factors, including the looming super El Niño weather effect, were adding to challenges facing developing countries, Banga said in an interview ahead of this week's annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion," Banga said, referring to the initial $25 billion plus another $35 billion that countries could tap by diverting resources from already approved World Bank projects.
"We'll see, but we're ready. We're engaged. We're having conversations with a number of them, you know, 30 to 40 countries are in dialogue with us," he said.
Many developing countries have been hit hard by the spike in energy prices and high interest rates that have increased borrowing costs at a time when their fiscal coffers are still depleted by measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic and the spike in inflation following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
World Bank estimates show that developing countries owe external creditors about $400 billion in 2026, with interest payments alone comprising one-third of the total.
Banga said more countries had shown interest in retooling existing projects than in tapping the immediate crisis window to address their liquidity needs. If the situation worsened, the Bank could make available as much as $100 billion in funds, he said, exceeding the $70 billion disbursed during the pandemic.
The World Bank last month announced that it attracted a [USN:L1N4580ZW TEXT:"record $112 billion in private capital"] in the year ended June versus $69 billion a year earlier, and more than triple the 2022 total before Banga, a former Mastercard CEO, became president.
That was on top of the $123 billion invested from the bank's own resources for that year, for a combined $235 billion, Banga said, underscoring the importance of tapping all available resources, especially at a time when Western countries have sharply cut official bilateral development aid.
"There is no one answer that fits when the world has these kinds of issues. What you need to do is figure out how to cut your coat to suit your cloth," Banga said.
Banga said he expected further gains in private capital flows in coming years, aided by expanded political risk guarantees from the bank's Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, growth in local currency financing, and continued work on regulatory reforms that made it easier for foreign investors.
The private capital jump was biggest in projects in upper-middle-income countries like Argentina or India, which accounted for $50 billion of the private capital, and lower-middle-income countries including Bangladesh and Angola, which accounted for $37 billion. But more work was needed to boost the roughly $3 billion in private capital flowing to low-income countries.
"In the smaller countries, it hasn't multiplied enough, and there are challenges," he said, noting the bank would announce some new initiatives this week aimed at ensuring micro-, small- and medium-sized businesses also had access to private capital.
Banga said private capital growth was also regionally spread, with the largest increase seen in Latin America and the Caribbean, which accounted for $36.3 billion of last year's total, followed by Europe and Central Asia with $21.3 billion, South Asia with $19.2 billion and Africa with $22 billion.
The top 10 recipient countries were Brazil, India, Turkey, Romania, Nigeria, Argentina, South Africa, Bangladesh, Mexico and Chile, the Bank said.
Banga said the World Bank and IMF were working together to address the high debt levels plaguing many developing countries through a series of initiatives, including efforts to boost countries' domestic revenue collections.
The Bank had already set up some debt-for-development swaps for Angola and Ivory Coast, and a portfolio-based guarantee for Argentina, and was working on over a dozen more projects.
"We've got 14 or 15 in the pipeline, helping them rotate out higher-priced old debt for newer-priced debt with our guarantees," with the difference then targeted at education, healthcare, water, or nature programs, he said.

items.title: La UE planea medidas para reducir a la mitad las importaciones de coches híbridos chinos
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Jenny Leonard, Alberto Nardelli
items.summary: Las medidas podrían entrar en vigor en diciembre y probablemente adoptarían la forma de contingentes arancelarios, que aplican un gravamen a las importaciones que superen un determinado volumen para f ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La Unión Europea tiene la intención de recurrir a medidas de salvaguardia para reducir a la mitad el número de importaciones de coches híbridos procedentes de China, según fuentes familiarizadas con las conversaciones. Ver más: Lista de autos nuevos que cuestan menos de US$25.000 El negociador jefe de comercio de la UE, Maros Sefcovic, informó a los funcionarios europeos de que el mecanismo para frenar las importaciones aún debe debatirse con los líderes del bloque la próxima semana, pero que es probable que se recurran a medidas de salvaguardia, según indicaron dichas fuentes, que hablaron bajo condición de anonimato. Si se aprueban, las medidas podrían entrar en vigor en diciembre, de acuerdo con una de las fuentes. Las medidas de salvaguardia suelen adoptar la forma de contingentes arancelarios, que aplican un gravamen a las importaciones que superen un determinado volumen para frenar los flujos excesivos. Esto cumpliría con las normas de la Organización Mundial del Comercio, y tanto China como la UE han señalado que ese es un requisito imprescindible. Sefcovic comunicó a los responsables que la medida reduciría el flujo de vehículos híbridos hacia la UE a unas 400.000 unidades al año, frente a las aproximadamente 800.000 previstas para 2026, según la misma fuente. Bloomberg informó anteriormente de que la UE estaba preparando medidas de salvaguardia para los vehículos híbridos. Un portavoz de la Comisión Europea, que se encarga de los asuntos comerciales de la UE, se negó a hacer comentarios. Los fabricantes de automóviles chinos, como Chery Automobile Co, han incrementado masivamente los envíos de vehículos a la UE en respuesta a la caída de su mercado nacional, lo que ha agravado la desaceleración que afecta a sus homólogos europeos, que se encuentran entre los que peor rendimiento registran a nivel mundial. Las ventas de automóviles de Mercedes-Benz Group AG cayeron un 8% en el tercer trimestre, mientras que Volkswagen AG recortó el mes pasado sus previsiones de beneficios tras una advertencia similar de BMW AG en junio. Sefcovic se reunió con el ministro de Comercio chino, Wang Wentao, en Pekín la semana pasada para analizar la situación, antes de emitir un comunicado conjunto en el que afirmaban haber alcanzado “un acuerdo sobre el comercio de vehículos híbridos conforme a las normas de la OMC”. El responsable de Comercio de la UE informará a los embajadores del bloque el domingo; posteriormente, los líderes de la UE se reunirán en Bruselas el jueves y el viernes para debatir los próximos pasos a seguir. El grupo de presión del sector automovilístico europeo, la ACEA, acogió con satisfacción el viernes el anuncio de un acuerdo provisional. “Una desestabilización brusca y repentina del mercado en Europa, junto con guerras de precios que reflejen la situación actual del mercado en China, sería muy perjudicial para la economía europea en su conjunto”, afirmó la directora general de la ACEA, Sigrid de Vries, en un comunicado . El auge de las ventas de coches híbridos chinos se ha convertido en un símbolo de la frustración de Europa con Pekín, pero no es más que una pequeña parte del problema general. Los líderes de la UE están preocupados por un déficit comercial que supera los 1.000 millones de euros (US$1.100 millones) al día y buscan formas de impedir que China inunde el continente con productos subvencionados y de bajo coste que socavan la industria local. “El déficit comercial supone un enorme desafío para la UE, que se deja sentir en todos los Estados miembros. Es insostenible y exige una vía creíble hacia el reequilibrio”, declaró Sefcovic a los periodistas el viernes en Pekín. “Debemos defender nuestras industrias y restablecer la igualdad de condiciones, que se ha visto distorsionada por el exceso de capacidad a nivel mundial”. El acuerdo tendrá una vigencia de cuatro años, según afirmó Sefcovic, aunque ninguna de las partes ofreció detalles sobre cómo moderarán las exportaciones de vehículos híbridos. Añadió que se reuniría con Wang en enero, antes de una nueva ronda de conversaciones prevista para marzo. En un comunicado, el Ministerio de Comercio chino señaló que ambas partes habían “reafirmado su compromiso, como socios comerciales clave, de gestionar adecuadamente las diferencias con arreglo a las normas de la OMC, mantener unas relaciones económicas y comerciales bilaterales estables y hacerlas más equilibradas”. Las ventas de coches híbridos chinos se han disparado, en parte porque eludieron los aranceles que la UE aplicará a los vehículos eléctricos a partir de 2024. En agosto, los coches de fabricación china representaron aproximadamente una cuarta parte de las ventas de híbridos en Europa. La UE tiene previsto utilizar los híbridos como caso de prueba que, de tener éxito, podría replicarse en otros sectores en los que el bloque detecta desequilibrios comerciales, según informó Bloomberg a principios de esta semana. De cara a las negociaciones de esta semana, Francia y Alemania han instado a la UE a ampliar significativamente sus competencias económicas de represalia, sugiriendo que debería incluso plantearse romper los lazos comerciales con aquellos países que desencadenan guerras comerciales. Las dos mayores economías de Europa también quieren que la UE investigue si las importaciones subvencionadas están perjudicando a sectores como el químico y el de los plásticos, investigaciones que podrían dar lugar a la imposición de más aranceles. La propuesta se consideró una táctica de presión dirigida contra Pekín, con la que Alemania respalda medidas contundentes a las que antes se había opuesto. Esta postura más firme refleja la creciente conciencia de Europa de que su déficit comercial con China, que alcanzó los 360.000 millones de euros el año pasado, está lastrando la industria local. Al mismo tiempo, sin embargo, China depende cada vez más de esas exportaciones para sustentar su propio crecimiento. “He venido aquí con un objetivo claro: empezar a reequilibrar la relación comercial entre la UE y China”, afirmó Sefcovic. items.title: Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
items.summary: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the ...
items.body:
Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:27 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:27 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.
The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. "Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."
"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days." A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.
"Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. "When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said.
LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well. "I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement.
"The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added. The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health.
The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health. Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17.
Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。

年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。
items.body:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。

年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。 期間中には２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の財務相・中央銀行総裁会議も開かれる。イランとの戦争が８カ月目に入り、エネルギー高によるインフレや公的債務の増大が議論の中心になる見通し。 

今年のＧ２０議長国を務める米国のベッセント財務長官は欠席し、財務省高官２人を派遣する。米政府当局者によると、国内で予定があるという。ウクライナ戦争や米国による国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）への制裁を巡って各国間の緊張が高まる中、ベッセント氏がＩＭＦ・世銀総会に加えてＧ２０会合も欠席することに、各国から不満が出る可能性がある。

世界銀行のアジェイ・バンガ総裁はロイターに、イランによるホルムズ海峡封鎖後も世界経済は懸念されたほど悪化していないものの、再び下押し圧力が強まっていると指摘した。

世界の石油供給の約２割が途絶し、軽油や肥料の価格が上昇。Ｇ７は軽油と原油計１億バレルを緊急備蓄から放出することで合意した。トランプ米大統領は１０日、ロシアから軽油の供給を受けることで合意したと発表し、対ロ制裁も一時的に免除する。この決定にはウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が強く反発した。

２月２８日の戦争開始以降、１０億バレルを超える石油が主に民間在庫から市場に放出されたが、業界幹部によると、世界市場に供給可能な在庫は減少しており、価格上昇への市場の脆弱性が増している。

バンガ氏は、エルニーニョ現象に加え、肥料価格やエネルギーコスト、債務問題が重なることが世界経済のリスクになるとして、今後数カ月に備え「一段と慎重になる必要がある」と述べた。ＩＭＦのゲオルギエワ専務理事も年次総会を前にした講演で「冬が来る」と警告した。

ＩＭＦは２０２６年の世界経済成長率を３％程度とする見通しを大きく変更しないもようだが、ウクライナや、イランの攻撃を受けエネルギー輸出が大幅に減少した湾岸諸国などは下方修正が予想される。

もう一つの大きな懸念は公的債務の増大だ。世界の公的債務は第２次世界大戦後で最高水準にあり、２０３０年までに世界の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）の１００％を超える見通し。新興国や低所得国では米金利上昇に伴う資本流出も重荷となっている。

途上国では利払い費が政府歳入の平均１０％をすでに超え、より高い金利での債務借り換えを迫られている。新型コロナ禍ではＧ２０が最貧国の債務返済猶予に動いたが、今回は同様の措置への機運は乏しい。

米シンクタンクのアトランティック・カウンシルで国際経済部門を統括するジョシュ・リプスキー氏は 、安全保障と国際金融の結び付きが一段と強まっていると指摘。地政学的危機が世界経済に急速に波及する中、政策当局は「もはや以前と同じ世界ではないことを認識しなければならない」と話す。

items.title: Kings C Maxime Raynaud exits preseason game with right knee injury
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud sustained an apparently serious right knee injury in the second quarter of a preseason loss to the host Golden State Warriors on Saturday night in San Francisco.
items.body:
Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud sustained an apparently serious right knee injury in the second quarter of a preseason loss to the host Golden State Warriors on Saturday night in San Francisco.
Raynaud was hurt while setting a screen for teammate Darius Acuff Jr. on Warriors guard Stephen Curry with 2:32 before halftime. As they collided, the 7-foot-1 center yelled in pain and crumpled to the floor. He was examined by medical staff and eventually was helped up, put in a wheelchair and exited the court to the locker room.
The second-year player got tests on the knee in Chase Center, including the X-ray room, at halftime. The Kings announced in the third quarter that he was out for the rest of the game with a right knee injury.
Sacramento did not have an update on his injury after the game, which Golden State won 111-106. Raynaud, 23, told reporters he was set to undergo an MRI late Saturday and was seen leaving the arena on crutches, per reports.
Raynaud collected 10 points, five rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes as a reserve on Saturday. He was 3-for-3 from the field, including 1-for-1 on 3-point attempts.
Sacramento selected the native of Paris in the second round of the 2025 NBA Draft out of Stanford. As a rookie, Raynaud averaged 12.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 26.5 minutes in 74 games (56 starts). He was selected to the All-Rookie second team.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Germany backs Ukraine's Zelenskiy after Trump's call for his removal
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more ...
items.body:
Germany backs Ukraine's Zelenskiy after Trump's call for his removal
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:20 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:20 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks. Wadephul said Germany remained by the side of Ukraine and its government "and fully support the President as he carries out his difficult duties."
The comments, at a leadership meeting of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), followed Trump's call on Saturday for Zelenskiy to be replaced and underlined Berlin's growing rift with Washington. Trump, who last week announced a diesel supply deal with Russia, called for Ukraine to replace Zelenskiy and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure.
Germany, the biggest European donor to Ukraine, said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia despite Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel. Wadephul, who met his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month, said "consistency and clarity" were needed to support Ukraine and bring Moscow to negotiate.
"We don't need less pressure, we need more pressure on Putin to make him be ready to negotiate," Wadephul said. "That is what this moment requires and that's what the government stands for." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskiy on Saturday and told him the UK would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia, a Downing Street spokesperson said.

items.title: Deutsche Bank chief warns German election results worrying foreign investors
items.summary: The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes. The AfD, which wants to ...
items.body:
Deutsche Bank chief warns German election results worrying foreign investors
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:13 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:13 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes. The AfD, which wants to restrict immigration and send asylum seekers home, scored some of its biggest-ever wins in eastern Germany last month. At the same time, the Left Party scored its biggest win in the election for the city government of Berlin, pledging to expropriate holdings of property companies.
"This poses a significant risk to Germany, and it should not be played down," Christian Sewing, chief executive of Deutsche Bank, told the Bild daily in an interview, referring to the rise of political extremes. "You can't expect a foreign investor to immediately draw a distinction between a state government and Germany as a whole," he said. "It's seen as Germany as a whole and I think that from an investor's point of view, that's understandable."
In the state of Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD, which is classified by security services as extremist in some regions, only narrowly fell short of an absolute majority in the state parliament, and it followed up two weeks later by taking first place in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The AfD has been accused by economists of fostering a climate that will drive away badly needed skilled workers and foreign investors.
The Left Party, meanwhile, vowed to tackle Berlin's soaring housing costs by expropriating the holdings of residential property companies. "And whether it's Saxony-Anhalt with the AfD or what's happening here in Berlin, it's anything but conducive to economic growth. And it's anything but investment-friendly," Sewing said.
He urged the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz to carry on with reforms to revive the economy. "That is the only response we have to the far-right and far-left extremists in this country," he said.

items.title: América empata y es líder general del torneo mexicano de fútbol
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: América, el club más ganador del fútbol mexicano con 16 títulos, empató el sábado como local ante Monterrey por 1-1 y se ubicó como líder general del torneo Apertura.
items.body:
América, el club más ganador del fútbol mexicano con 16 títulos, empató el sábado como local ante Monterrey por 1-1 y se ubicó como líder general del torneo Apertura.
Con la igualada en la undécima jornada, las "Águilas" del América llegaron a 21 puntos en lo más alto de la tabla general, donde le siguen Toluca y Querétaro con 20 unidades.
En el partido, disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, los "Rayados" de Monterrey se pusieron en ventaja a los 18 minutos con un vistoso remate de volea del uruguayo Diego Rossi en el área tras un preciso centro enviado por Orbelín Pineda desde el sector derecho.
América empató en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte cuando el defensa uruguayo Santiago Bueno definió de derecha en el área chica después de que el portero argentino Estebán Andrada rechazó un remate de Henry Martín.
En la segunda parte, ambos equipos salieron en busca del triunfo, generando llegadas de peligro en las dos áreas que no concretaron.
América estuvo cerca de dar la vuelta al marcador a los 79 minutos con un potente disparo del colombiano Miguel Borja que se estrelló en el travesaño.
El delantero colombiano fue expulsado a los 87 minutos tras cometer una fuerte falta sobre el defensa Carlos Salcedo.
En los otros partidos del sábado, Querétaro ganó 2-0 al Atlante con goles del uruguayo Santiago Homenchenko y Denilson Muñoz.
Atlas y Guadalajara empataron 1-1. Para los "Rojinegros" del Atlas anotó el argentino Kevin Zenón, mientras que para las "Chivas" de Guadalajara lo hizo Ángel Sepúlveda.
En tanto, Bravos de Ciudad Juárez y Tijuana empataron 1-1 con goles del brasileño Rodrigo Dourado y del marroquí naturalizado español Mourad Daoudi.
La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Atlético de San Luis juegue ante Santos Laguna, Pachuca enfrente a Necaxa y el vigente campeón Cruz Azul visite a Pumas UNAM.
El viernes, Tigres UANL venció por 3-2 a Toluca, mientras que Puebla y León empataron 1-1.
