items.title: Barcelona cruise past Getafe, Real Madrid stutter to win over Villarreal
items.author: Ruairidh Barlow
items.creator: Ruairidh Barlow
items.summary: Barcelona extended their perfect LaLiga start with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Getafe on Saturday before Real Madrid overcame Villarreal 1-0 despite having Vinicius Jr sent off.
items.body:
Barcelona extended their perfect LaLiga start with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Getafe on Saturday before Real Madrid overcame Villarreal 1-0 despite having Vinicius Jr sent off.
Barca's victory makes it eight wins for Hansi Flick's side and maintains their five-point lead at the top over Atletico Madrid, who won 2-1 at Alaves with a late Cristian Romero goal.
Real Madrid's narrow win keeps them in third place on 18 points, six points off the pace set by their arch-rivals, but Jose Mourinho is no closer to improving their performances.
The three-week international break did little to disrupt Barcelona’s rhythm and they went ahead after two minutes when Anthony Gordon cut inside and saw his shot deflect off Getafe midfielder Mario Martin and beyond goalkeeper David Soria.
The visitors struggled to escape their own half under sustained pressure and Gabriel Jesus punished a giveaway by Zaid Romero to score on the half-hour in his first start for Barca.
The hosts remained firmly in control after the break, with Getafe testing Joan Garcia only once on the keeper’s return from injury.
Jules Kounde, who missed a clear chance in the first half, completed the scoring for Barca in the 73rd minute with a simple finish from Lamine Yamal’s curling cross.
MBAPPE HITS THE POST Real had the clearer first-half openings against Villarreal, with Kylian Mbappe's seventh-minute shot hitting the post.
They remained unconvincing on the ball, although neither side was able to direct proceedings. Villarreal were equally imprecise with their passes and chances were in short supply.
The tempo increased in the second half and Yan Diomande scored the winner when he beat the offside trap in the 63rd minute and found the bottom corner of the net. It was the Ivory Coast forward's first goal for Real since joining in August.
A forlorn Vinicius Jr watched 19-year-old Diomande in the Brazilian's preferred left-wing position from the bench in the first half but was bright when he came on after 52 minutes to replace wing back Trent Alexander-Arnold.
Eight minutes after the opener, Vinicius thought he had scored Real's second, with Mourinho jogging to the goal-line to celebrate with the substitute.
However, after a VAR review, the goal was chalked off and Vinicius was sent off for pulling substitute Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up.
An open game ensued, with Villarreal's Peter Gulacsi and Real's Thibaut Courtois making excellent saves. In the closing stages, the frustrated visitors could not stretch their 10-man hosts sufficiently to find gaps in their backline.
The fiery reaction to Vinicius' sending off from Mourinho and his players infused Real's defending with extra intensity, and a positive rearguard effort was rewarded with a clean sheet.
Mourinho did not attend his post-match press conference, with no reason given by the club. The Portuguese now begins preparations for Real's next game at AS Roma in the Champions League as he searches for a consistent pattern of play.
ATLETICO GRAB LATE WINNER Atletico's Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring against Alaves after a brilliant interchange with Jonathan David before a Lucas Boye penalty for the hosts in first-half stoppage time.
But Angel Perez was sent off for Alaves in the 61st minute and Atletico's pressure told three minutes from time, with central defender Romero scoring from a deft Alex Baena assist.
Rayo Vallecano's home clash with Athletic Club was [USN:L6N45W02X TEXT:"abandoned due to fan protests"] at Vallecas Stadium.

items.title: Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike released from hospital, returned to prison
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Governor Bill Lee has suspended all executions for the rest of the year.
items.body:
Death row inmate Christa Pike was released from a US hospital on Saturday and sent back to prison where she will continue receiving medical care following her [USN:L1N45M031 TEXT:"botched execution attempt in Tennessee"], her attorneys said.
Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years, said attorneys Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen from Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee, and Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason from the Tennessee Office of the Post Conviction Defender in a joint release.
Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in the hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving the attempted execution on September 30, her lawyers said on Wednesday. They previously believed she could be brain-dead.
Pike, 50, had been taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two injections failed to kill her at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution.
A Tennessee judge this week [USN:L1N45T0M9 TEXT:"ordered"] state officials to preserve all evidence related to their failed attempt to execute her, a development one of [USN:L1N45T0M9 TEXT:"her lawyers"] called the "first of many steps to preserve and enforce her constitutional rights."
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look in to the botched execution of Pike and a similar failure involving Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous lines.

"To day , Russia said thank you for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, in some of his sharpest criticism yet of the White House.
Zaporizhzhia has been a regular target of Russian bombardment with strikes intensifying in the past few months.
A 6-year-old girl was among those killed when one strike reduced part of an apartment block to rubble. Her grandfather, Anatoliy Chumniy, stood sobbing over her body, laid on the ground in a white bag, after rescuers pulled it from the wreckage.

"Her birth day would have been at the end of the month," he said through tears.
Eighteen others were wounded in the attack on the industrial city , with a pre-war population of over 700,000 and whose outskirts lie less than 30 km (20 miles) from the front line.

Rescuers evacuate wounded residents, Yana and her husband Anton, found under debris of an apartment building damaged during a Russian air strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine October 10, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer

A woman reacts after pulling her relatives from the rubble of a residential building destroyed by a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Kateryna Klochko)

RUSSIA ESCALATING ATTACK S ON UKRAINIAN CITIES It was the third mass-casualty attack on Ukraine this week.
Nearly 80 civilians were killed in Russian strikes on Wednes day and Thurs day , including at least 30 killed by a bomb in the eastern garrison city of Kramatorsk and 22 others by a missile in the town of Pryluky, 80 miles east of Kyiv.
A senior official in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, said Russia had hit several locations simultaneously in the early hours of Satur day .
Rescuers clambered through crumbled masonry to pull other residents of the building out alive. One man, whose leg was trapped in the rubble, screamed in pain as he was being freed.
"If (the Russian s) have money, they’ll be able to carry on fighting us," said Nataliia Malysheva, a 49-year-old local resident whose parents died in hospital after being pulled from the rubble.
"How many lives have been lost here, how many homes have been destroyed? How many innocent people have died in the meantime?"

Related:

Russian strike on buses kills 30 in frontline Ukrainian city

MOSCOW NEEDS 'DIFFERENT SIGNALS' "Last night provided yet more confirmation that Russia perceives any easing of pressure as a signal that it can supposedly keep fighting, that it can supposedly keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed," Zelenskyy said.
A missile attack on Satur day after noon also hit a restaurant, wounding seven people in Kyiv.
Russian drones flew over Kyiv throughout the day , part of a vast new wave of bombardment of the capital, the heaviest since the early day s of the war.
Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Satur day its drones had struck a data-processing centre in Kyiv and a cargo ship carrying military supplies to the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

Read more:

Commentary: Russia’s new jet‑powered drones mark latest evolution in air war above Ukraine

TRUMP LIFTS DIESEL SANCTIONS Trump 's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports comes as his administration seeks to curb fuel prices, which have risen sharply during the US conflict with Iran.
Kyiv had instead urged Washington to increase pressure on Moscow in an effort to force it into serious negotiations to end the four-and-a-half-year war.
Trump , meanwhile, has criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, which he claims have driven up global prices. Kyiv has said it wants a total halt on all energy strikes by both sides as Moscow pummels Ukraine's power grid.
On Satur day , parts of Kyiv and the surrounding region were left without power, bringing the city 's metro trains to a complete halt for the second time this week.
The latest strikes came after Ukrainian and European officials held talks with US negotiators in Miami on Fri day aimed at developing a common proposal for ending the war, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Related:

Trump says Putin agrees to major release of diesel to US, global markets

Trump announced the diesel deal while the negotiations were underway, a move Zelenskiy said had caught Kyiv by surprise.
The Ukrainian delegation was headed home on Satur day , presidential aide Dmytro Lytvyn was cited by the Interfax Ukraine news agency as saying.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Trump that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attack s on Moscow .
US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Moscow within the next two weeks, Russian state news agency TASS reported on Satur day , citing a source.
Four civilians were killed and five others were wounded as a result of Ukrainian attack s on the Russian -controlled Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine, the Russian -installed governor said on Satur day .
Reuters could not independently verify the report and there was no immediate comment from Ukraine.

items.title: Erie, Pennsylvania shooter killed 8 people, then himself, police say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A 45-year-old man shot and killed eight people, including a pregnant woman and two children, then apparently shot himself to death, authorities said.
items.body:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed eight people in Erie, Pennsylvania, including a pregnant woman and two children, then apparently shot himself to death, authorities said on Saturday at a press conference where they revealed details of the previous evening's shooting.
The shooter, who has yet to be identified, died of an apparent self-inflicted wound before officers arrived on the scene, said Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah.
"Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said.
Police have yet to establish a motive, Lorah said. He said eight of the nine who died in the shooting were family members, and one was a family friend.
Lorah said after the shooter entered the home, he came out of the house and shot two women who appeared "distressed" and were pacing back and forth seeking assistance from neighbors.
Police found the suspect on the second floor of the home on Perry Street, Lorah said.
Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said the police department "arrived at a horrific scene, faced unimaginable circumstances, and carried out their duties with courage and professionalism."
"They too are members of this community, and they too will carry the weight of what happened last night," she said.
Earlier, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said in a statement on X that he had spoken with Mayor Devlin and had offered support following "the tragic mass shooting."
Shapiro has long advocated for "common sense gun safety," and pushed the Pennsylvania General Assembly in 2024 to pass gun reforms, including universal background checks and restrictions on ghost guns, which are homemade guns that lack serial numbers and cannot be traced. Several of Shapiro’s proposals have stalled in the state legislature.
There have been more than 400 mass shootings in the US in 2026, according to data compiled by Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as one in which four or more people are shot, excluding the shooter. The last recorded mass shootings in Pennsylvania took place in July in Philadelphia, according to the data.

items.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico coast
items.author: Daniel Becerril, Alberto Fajardo
items.creator: Daniel Becerril, Alberto Fajardo
items.summary: Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday.
items.body:
Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday, threatening destructive winds, storm surges and potentially deadly flooding as it approaches landfall.
The US National Hurricane Center said Simon was located about 115 miles (185 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, on Saturday morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph) as it moved northward.
Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane late on Saturday or early Sunday, and some additional strengthening remains possible before landfall, the NHC said.
A hurricane warning was in effect for portions of Mexico's Pacific coast south of the beach resort of Puerto Vallarta, including the area around Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port. A tropical storm watch was in effect farther south toward Lazaro Cardenas.
The NHC urged residents in the warning area, which also includes the Islas Marias archipelago offshore, to rush preparations to protect life and property.
“Simon has strengthened incredibly quickly, and that’s what makes storms like this so dangerous,” said AccuWeather meteorologist Dan Pydynowski.
“Strong winds could damage homes and businesses, while flooding and mudslides could wash out roads and make it difficult for emergency crews to reach some communities. Even after the storm passes, power outages and damaged infrastructure could make recovery challenging.”
PREPARATIONS UNDER WAY IN MANZANILLO In the early afternoon on Saturday in Manzanillo, residents appeared largely calm despite the approaching storm, with little sign of panic buying at supermarkets, according to a Reuters reporter on the ground. Some stores had begun boarding up their windows, while businesses were closing and streets were relatively empty. Rain had been falling intermittently since late on Friday, and rising seas were pushing waves almost to the entrances of beachfront hotels, although strong winds had yet to arrive.
Civil protection workers had closed beaches, erected barriers and raised red and black warning flags, urging residents to stay away from the shore. Marines, soldiers, National Guard officers and emergency personnel were patrolling areas vulnerable to flooding and landslides, while authorities had begun precautionary evacuations in parts of Cihuatlan, a flood-prone municipality in neighboring Jalisco state, near Manzanillo. Rivers in some areas were already running high, raising concerns they could overflow if heavy rains intensified.
Mexican authorities warned that heavy rainfall was expected in the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.
UP TO 30 INCHES OF RAIN EXPECTED The NHC said Simon was expected to produce 10 to 20 inches (25 to 51 cm) of rain across portions of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals of up to 30 inches (76 cm) possible in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. The rainfall could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in mountainous areas.
A storm surge is expected along the coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall, accompanied by large and destructive waves, the NHC said. Swells generated by Simon are expected to affect portions of Mexico's southwestern and west-central coast over the coming days, creating dangerous surf and rip current conditions.
Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday.
Last week, Hurricane Polo made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.

items.body:
El tercer ataque contra el aeropuerto internacional de Riad este seman dejó al menos 12 muertos y más de 300 heridos, dijeron las autoridades sauditas, mientras que los hutíes se adjudicaron la importante escalada del conflicto más activo vinculado a la guerra con Irán.
Entre los fallecidos hubo cuatro sauditas, dos bangladesíes y ciudadanos de Estados Unidos, Jordania, Palestina, Siria, Sudán y Egipto, informó la autoridad de aviación civil saudita. El recuento de heridos era de 309.
Los hospitales se vieron desbordados por los heridos trasladados en ambulancias y helicópteros, dijeron fuentes cercanas al asunto. Algunos se encontraban en estado crítico.
Fue el tercer ataque en menos de una semana contra el aeropuerto. Los dos anteriores dejaron cuatro muertos y causaron graves daños a un avión comercial saudita estacionado en la pista.
La ola de ataques mortales ha puesto de manifiesto las vulnerabilidades del reino, mientras libra una campaña aérea contra los hutíes para apoyar la guerra terrestre del Gobierno yemení contra el grupo respaldado por Irán.
Arabia Saudita y el Gobierno yemení han reivindicado cientos de ataques contra objetivos en territorio controlado por los hutíes, los que, según estos últimos, causaron la muerte de civiles, entre ellos mujeres y niños.
Reuters no pudo verificar de forma independiente las afirmaciones.
No hubo aviso previo del ataque al aeropuerto del sábado y el sistema de alerta de amenazas de Arabia Saudita no emitió ninguna.
Todos los vuelos procedentes de Riad fueron desviados el sábado, y las operaciones en el aeropuerto, que da servicio a una ciudad de aproximadamente 8 millones de habitantes, quedaron temporalmente suspendidas, dijo la autoridad de aviación civil saudita .
El jefe de la oficina de prensa de los hutíes dijo en una publicación en X tras el ataque que el grupo había "paralizado el aeropuerto internacional de Riad".
Los hutíes han instado a los aviones comerciales a evitar el espacio aéreo saudita, declarándolo zona de operaciones militares después de que el Gobierno yemení, respaldado por Arabia Saudita, lanzó una ofensiva contra el grupo el lunes.
Tras el ataque, se le preguntó al presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, si Estados Unidos tenía previsto sumarse a la ofensiva saudita contra los hutíes.
"Es posible. Lo vamos a estudiar. Acabamos de enterarnos del reciente ataque, así que tomaremos una decisión. Actuamos con gran rapidez", dijo.
HERIDOS EN EL SUELO Uno de los testigos presenciales dijo haber visto una explosión y, a continuación, varias personas heridas tendidas en el suelo dentro del aeropuerto. Más de una decena de ambulancias se dirigieron a toda prisa hacia el aeropuerto.
Un viajero herido contó a Reuters que vio algo volando por el cielo fuera del aeropuerto antes de que se derrumbara parte del techo cerca de una puerta de embarque.
La página web de seguimiento de vuelos flightradar24 mostraba que todos los vuelos con destino a Riad habían sido desviados o cancelados, y que, en un momento dado, solo un helicóptero sobrevolaba el aeropuerto.
Los ataques de los hutíes del jueves y de principios de semana ya habían provocado que varias compañías aéreas suspendieran o cancelaran sus servicios a la capital saudita, poco antes de que Riad acoja importantes conferencias sobre energía e inversión.

items.title: Rayo-Athletic match abandoned after fans protest against club owner
items.author: David Latona
items.creator: David Latona
items.summary: The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
items.body:
The LaLiga match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after home fans lobbed paper airplanes and small rubber balls onto the pitch in protest against the Madrid club's owner midway through the first half.
The game was the first of this league season played at the Estadio de Vallecas, which was temporarily [USN:L1N43U0P3 TEXT:"closed"] after an audit found serious safety issues.
Rayo fans blame negligence by club owner Raul Martin Presa, who in turn accused regional authorities of deliberately targeting his club.
The Sports Association of Rayo Vallecano fan group said in a statement after the suspension that their protest was "legitimate and democratic... necessary and peaceful."
It added that it was the "consequence of three decades of putting the safety and health of 15,000 people at risk every fortnight".
La Liga said in a statement on social media it "strongly condemned this type of behaviour, which endangers safety and makes the normal development of the competition impossible".
A new date and time for the match will be announced shortly, LaLiga said. Athletic returned to Bilbao, saying on social media that LaLiga had communicated the game would not take place later on Saturday or on Sunday.
Last season's Conference League finalists Rayo released a statement saying the club would seek to identify and discipline those responsible, adding that the forced postponement was part of a sustained campaign of disruption by the fan group.
The players, officials and supporters present were "victims of an attack on their rights and freedoms, committed by an organised group of intolerant individuals," said the statement.
"UNSUSTAINABLE SITUATION" Rayo captain Oscar Valentin said on social media that "an unsustainable situation had reached its limit" and too little had been done to prevent things getting to this point.
"It is necessary to listen to and understand the discontent of our fans. We need a way of bringing ALL parties closer together, always putting the common good first and, above all, the good of Rayo Vallecano," Valentin added.
After Rayo's first three home games were moved to the stadium of second-tier Leganes, registering some of La Liga's lowest-ever attendance figures, home fans started chanting, jeering and whistling against Presa before kickoff on Saturday.
By the 13th minute - when Rayo ultras usually chant the song "Presa leave already" - hundreds of fans launched paper planes and small rubber balls onto the pitch, prompting the referee to suspend play.
A 15-minute pause ensued, during which the stadium's speaker urged spectators not to throw objects onto the field as staff hastily removed them.
When play resumed a little later, fans in the south stand again hurled objects onto the pitch and the referee abandoned the game.
Anger at Presa's management has [USN:L8N3NH005 TEXT:"reached a peak"] in recent months, following the closure of Vallecas Stadium for Rayo's opening home games of the season.
In a friendly against Cagliari last Saturday, anti-Presa graffiti appeared in the VIP box, which fans surrounded in protest before leaving the stadium.

items.title: Houthi strike on Saudi airport kills 12, worst attack on kingdom in a decade
items.author: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Enas Alashray
items.summary: At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer.
items.body:
At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer.
The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.
President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, some in critical condition after the attack, which occurred without warning.
CONFLICT ESCALATES AFTER YEMEN WAR CEASEFIRE UNRAVELS The two previous attacks on King Khalid International Airport this week killed four and caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac. The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as it wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the Iran-backed group.
The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for the attack, but a Saudi-led military coalition vowed to respond.
Trump, asked whether the US planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, told reporters: "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the attacks on the airport, saying they "demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life". UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also condemned Saturday's strike, reiterating that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure violate international law and must cease immediately.
Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes on targets in Houthi-held territory. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
The Saudis entered the Yemen war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to force the Houthis out of the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The war became a bloody stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine.
A 2022 ceasefire reached by the Saudis and the Houthis unravelled this summer, culminating in a lightning Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces.
EXPLOSION, PEOPLE ON GROUND, AMBULANCES RUSHING The Saudi-backed Yemeni government began an offensive this week to try to retake that territory, but it has made only slow gains, even as the Houthis put the country's third-largest city, Taiz, under siege.
On Saturday, all flights were diverted from Riyadh and operations at the airport that serves a city of 8 million people were suspended, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
The head of the Houthi media office posted on X that the group had "shut down Riyadh international airport". The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations.
The Houthis have warned international airlines against operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying it has become a theatre of their military operations, with the exception of airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
An eyewitness at the airport reported seeing an explosion and then multiple people lying injured on the ground inside. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing towards the facility. A video verified by Reuters showed ambulances at the airport.
An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.
The US embassy in Riyadh said it "strongly recommends all US citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."
Earlier Houthi attacks had prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"major energy and investment conferences."] Organizers of those conferences said ahead of the strikes on Saturday they would go ahead as planned.

items.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended after national team walkout, media reports say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
items.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after disciplinary proceedings were opened over the forward's departure from the national team camp, Portuguese media reported on Saturday.
The 41-year-old left the squad's base in [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"Copenhagen"] before Portugal's Nations League match against Denmark last week, after a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo, an unused substitute against Norway, [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"accused Jesus"] of twice breaking his word regarding his role in the team.
After Portugal's 2-1 win, Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player but left the door open for his return.
According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the FPF confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened against Ronaldo.
"Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status," the federation was quoted as saying.
FPF president Pedro Proenca said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.
"The Portuguese Football Federation and its president, in this spirit of tranquility, speaking with all parties, who have already publicly demonstrated their desire to have the captain back with us, there is an expressed wish from everyone," he was quoted as saying by A Bola.
"This includes the federation, the FPF president, the national team coach, the captain and the players."
Regarding Ronaldo's disciplinary process, Proenca added: "That will depend solely on the Disciplinary Committee, which is an autonomous body, and it will do its job."
Ronaldo apologised on Tuesday for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway game and for leaving his teammates, adding that he would remain available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

items.title: Guimaraes grabs winner as Arsenal rally to beat Leeds
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
items.body:
Arsenal came back from a goal down to beat Leeds United 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, with Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes coming off the bench to net the winner as the Premier League resumed following a lengthy international break.
The competition returned under a cloud, with Manchester City found guilty by an independent commission of more than 100 breaches of the [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"league's financial rules"] over nine years and their failure to co-operate with the investigation.
City have denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the decision.
On the pitch, champions Arsenal climbed to second in the table on 15 points, behind City on goal difference before the Manchester club travel to Liverpool on Sunday.
Chelsea struck twice in the opening three minutes en route to a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, with Jordan Henderson and Joao Pedro bagging two goals apiece, and are fifth on 10 points.
Tottenham Hotspur struck in stoppage time to salvage a 1-1 draw at Manchester United as both sides' struggles continued.
Brighton & Hove Albion climbed to third, two points off top spot, with a 2-0 win at Sunderland.
Aston Villa and visiting Brentford drew 2-2, while Ipswich Town edged Fulham 2-1 at Portman Road with a last-gasp goal to leave the last-placed London side without a league victory this season.
FRUSTRATING FIRST HALF Arsenal were looking to bounce back, having slumped to a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in the last game before the break but endured a frustrating first half as they struggled to create chances.
Their play improved in the second period, but Leeds took the lead in the 55th minute when James Justin slammed home a clever pull-back from Gabriel Gudmundsson.
Riccardo Calafiori levelled for Arsenal seven minutes later, the Italian jumping to steer home Ben White's knock-down and, sensing his side could grab all three points, manager Mikel Arteta rang the changes.
He sent on Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres, and was rewarded when Guimaraes grabbed the winner with a brilliantly worked goal in the 70th minute, sending a low shot into the far corner of the net from the edge of the box.
"It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said.
"I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded."
Leeds are sixth on nine points.
UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score.
Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva.
Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick.
Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022.
At Old Trafford, Spurs were the better team but United punished their wastefulness in the 73rd minute when Matheus Cunha picked out Bryan Mbeumo in the box, and Mbeumo slotted home with United's second shot on target.
Rodrigo Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a 78th-minute melee.
But 10-man Spurs equalised in the 92nd minute when Dominic Solanke got away from Lisandro Martinez to nod Sandro Tonali's cross home for a well-deserved leveller that got them off the bottom of the table. They are 18th on three points, while United are 12th with six points.
Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute.
Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa.
Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
items.author: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
items.summary: The Palestinian president blamed Israel, whose foreign minister rejected his remarks as a lie.
items.body:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability."
There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009.
The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November.
In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize.
The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process.
PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections.
An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions.
The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms.
Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025.
France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

items.title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed, organisers say, despite deadly airport attack
items.author: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
items.summary: The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after missile attacks on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week.
items.body:
The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after [USN:L1N45V07H TEXT:"missile attacks"] on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week.
The attacks led to widespread flight disruptions, with people taking land routes or circuitous alternative flights. The UK, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh.
Riyadh is sticking to plans to convene global events and trying to draw in investment even amid escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen that has seen the kingdom attacked dozens of times over the past weeks.
Organisers of the World Petroleum Congress, set to host top global oil executives and policymakers from Sunday to Thursday, said it would proceed as planned with foreign leaders and ministers in attendance, an email sent to delegates said.
"Your comfort is our priority," it said, noting that alternative routes to Riyadh, including via a four-hour drive from Dammam on the kingdom's eastern coast, were available.
Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin on Friday said he would not fly to Riyadh for the International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting, an event on WPC's sidelines, but would participate via video link.
The Future Investment Initiative, launched by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as the kingdom's flagship investment conference a decade ago, would also proceed as planned from October 26-29, organisers said.
"Safety and well-being remain our highest priority," a statement attributed to FII CEO Maha Al Saud said.
"Comprehensive security measures will be in place at Riyadh's airports, our conference venues and official hotels, with coordinated arrangements for participants' transportation," it said.
Chief executives of some of the world's biggest financial institutions such as JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon and Citi's Jane Fraser were on the list of expected attendees. Citi and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.
Germany's Lufthansa has suspended Riyadh flights through October 16 while Gulf carriers Etihad Airways and Flydubai have cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital scheduled for October 10.
Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.

items.title: 「台湾は中国の一部」、中国が台湾総統の演説非難
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［北京　１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［北京　１０日　ロイター］ - 中国国務院台湾事務弁公室は１０日、台湾の頼清徳総統が同日行った双十節（建国記念日）の演説について、「事実を無視し、真実をゆがめ、民衆を惑わし、下心をあらわにしている」と非難した。

同弁公室は、頼氏が演説で「『台湾独立』の分裂主義思想にかたくなに固執」し、「中国本土の脅威」を誇張したと指摘した。その上で「世界に中国は一つしかなく、台湾は中国の一部だ。これこそが台湾海峡の真の現状だ」と主張した。

台湾の将来についても「台湾同胞を含む全ての中国人民が共同で決定することができ、またそうでなければならない」と述べた。

頼清徳総統は演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。

items.title: From 'cockroach' post to protest leader: India's Dipke tests Modi government
items.author: Tora Agarwala
items.creator: Tora Agarwala
items.summary: His six-word reply to the Supreme Court's chief justice shot him to fame.
items.body:
Indian police detained on Saturday Abhijeet Dipke, the political strategist who turned a "cockroach" jibe at unemployed youth into a nationwide protest movement that helped force the resignation of a federal minister.
Police met Dipke's aircraft as it landed in the capital of New Delhi ahead of a rally demanding the resignation of the election chief over accusations of [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"voter list manipulation"] that critics say dropped about 130 million voters from a draft roll.
"I have come to be arrested, arrest me ... I am not afraid of you guys," Dipke told police officers aboard the aircraft, in television images that showed one of them assuring him he was not being arrested, but rather that his cooperation was sought.
Dipke, 31, born in a Dalit family on the lower rungs of India's caste system, shot to fame this year after his six-word response to Supreme Court Chief Justice Surya Kant's remarks likening unemployed youth to "cockroaches" went viral online.
The post spawned the satirical "Cockroach Janta Party", an online movement that rapidly evolved into a political force.
It mobilised mass street protests that culminated in the July resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, a rare exit from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's cabinet, following sustained public pressure.
Dipke's detention came after he called for a [USN:L1N45W00K TEXT:"fresh protest"] on Saturday seeking the resignation of election commission chief [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over the changes.
The election panel says the figure, which is larger than the population of Japan, comprises entries flagged during draft revision, and that voters wrongly removed can enroll again.
Bearded and usually wearing T-shirt and jeans, Dipke had led a protest in the southern tech hub of Bengaluru before travelling via Mumbai to the capital, where police detained him with two senior group leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.
Despite a police crackdown in Delhi and tight protest restrictions, Dipke urged supporters to demonstrate peacefully, citing the example of Mahatma Gandhi, India's apostle of non-violence.
"I don't know what will happen tomorrow," Dipke said in a video recorded before Saturday's flight. "But one thing I am sure of is that I am not going to be afraid. Neither am I going to step back. We have to save our democracy."
Authorities called in thousands of security forces to fortify Delhi, with travel and telecoms links suspended, in a [USN:L1N45W00K TEXT:"lockdown"] designed to stop the youth protest.
"Why is the prime minister so scared of the country's youth, the country's people?" Dipke asked before his flight.
UNLIKELY EVENTS SET OFF BY SIX-WORD POST "What if all cockroaches come together?" was Dipke's question in a May social media post that almost overnight turned the political communications professional into one of the most recognisable faces of India's youth protest movement.
He returned to India after completing a master's degree in public relations in the United States, saying his viral success had given him "a chance to do actual, meaningful work", despite threats he and his family received.
The "Cockroach Janta Party" amassed millions of followers online and helped drive protests over leaks of a medical entrance examination paper affecting about 2 million candidates.
The movement eventually focused its anger on Pradhan, who resigned on July 25.
Since then, Dipke and his supporters, who see the group as a political pressure movement rather than a party, have campaigned on issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs for young people.
It returned to the streets after a report last month in the Indian Express newspaper.
The paper said two of election chief Kumar's deputies had repeatedly raised concerns about voter-roll revisions, registration procedures and the commission's digital systems.
The poll body has said differing views are normal during internal deliberations.
(This story has been corrected to fix the spelling of Abhijeet Dipke's first name in paragraph 1.)

items.title: ゴキブリ党創設者ら拘束、選管トップ抗議封じ込め　インド首都厳戒
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Saurabh Sharma　Aftab Ahmed　Sakshi Dayal

[ニューデリー １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Saurabh Sharma　Aftab Ahmed　Sakshi Dayal

[ニューデリー １０日 ロイター] - インドの警察は１０日、若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」の創設者、アビジート・ディプケ氏を拘束した。首都ニューデリーで予定されていた抗議集会を阻止し、参加者や野党の幹部らも拘束した。警察官や準軍事組織の要員数千人が投入され、首都は厳戒態勢にある。

ニューデリーでは、有権者名簿の見直しに関して不正があったとして選挙管理委員会委員長の辞任を求める抗議集会が予定されていた。当局は、抗議集会が始まる前に一帯を封鎖した。

ディプケ氏は抗議集会に参加するため、ムンバイからデリーに到着した航空機内で警察に拘束された。ＣＪＰは指導者らに対する「権威主義的な拘束」を非難。１０日の集会を率いる指導部を機能不全に陥れるための「事前に計画された足止め」だとして、即時釈放を求めた。

テレビ各局の映像によると、野党議員数人、西ベンガル州首相を務めたママタ・バナジー氏やデリー首都圏首相を務めたアルビンド・ケジリワル氏も拘束された。

デジタルニュースメディア２社の代表者によると、デモを取材していた両社の記者計４人が警察に一時拘束された。ロイターの記者１人も拘束されたが、その後、解放された。

最高裁判所の弁護士会会長は、最高裁前で抗議していた弁護士数人が連行されたが、その後解放されたと述べた。

一連の拘束について、警察からのコメントは得られていない。

治安部隊が主要道路や市内への入り口に検問所を設置しした。主要道路には催涙ガス銃を搭載した暴動鎮圧車両が配備され、警官が車両を検査している。ビジネス街ではインターネット接続が遮断され、数十の地下鉄駅や市場が閉鎖されたが、小規模なデモが行われたもようだ。

items.title: Trump calls for replacing Ukraine's Zelenskiy in tussle over diesel deal with Russia
items.author: Max Hunder, Steve Holland
items.creator: Max Hunder, Steve Holland
items.summary: In some of his harshest criticism yet of the White House, Ukraine's president linked the US lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel with a Russian attack that killed 20 people, including three children, in Zaporizhzhia.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump on Saturday called for Ukraine to replace its leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, a day after announcing a diesel supply deal with Russia that had drawn a sharp rebuke from Zelenskiy.
In some of his [USN:L1N45W01L TEXT:"harshest criticism"] yet of the White House, Zelenskiy linked the US lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel with a Russian attack on Saturday that killed 20 people, including 3 children, in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia.
A steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of next month's midterm elections, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress.
"I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump told reporters at the White House, saying Zelenskiy had hurt global diesel supplies with strikes on Russian refineries.
"He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world."
ZELENSKIY SAYS DIESEL DEAL EMBOLDENS RUSSIA Earlier in the day, Zelenskiy said Trump's announcement on Friday of the diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin had emboldened Moscow. Kyiv has instead urged Washington to pressure Moscow for serious negotiations to end the 4-1/2-year-old war .
The Russian government said on Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports.
"Today, Russia said thank you for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskiy said.
"Last night provided yet more confirmation that Russia perceives any easing of pressure as a signal that it can supposedly keep fighting, that it can supposedly keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed."
The southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia has been a regular target of Russian bombardment with [USN:L6N44312E TEXT:"strikes intensifying"] in the past few months.
On Saturday, a 6-year-old girl was among those killed in Zaporizhzhia when one strike reduced part of an apartment block to rubble. Her grandfather, Anatoliy Chumniy, stood sobbing over her body, laid on the ground in a white bag, after rescuers pulled it from the wreckage.
"Her birthday would have been at the end of the month," he said through tears.
It was the third mass-casualty attack on Ukraine this week.
Nearly 80 civilians were killed in Russian strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, including at least 30 killed by a bomb in the eastern garrison city of Kramatorsk and 22 others by a missile in the town of Pryluky, about 130 km (80 miles) east of Kyiv.
The diesel deal was also criticized by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions that Congress had recently passed, not lift them.
Analysts said the agreement was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices, with the volumes still much lower than what Russia usually exports when its refineries are not under attack.
BRITAIN VOWS TO STRENGTHEN RUSSIA SANCTIONS British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskiy on Saturday and said [USN:FWN45V15A TEXT:"Britain would strengthen"] its sanctions on Russia, according to a Downing Street spokesperson, who added that the two leaders would meet in person in the coming days.
The latest strikes followed talks between Ukrainian and European officials with US negotiators in Miami on Friday, which were aimed at developing a common [USN:L1N45V11A TEXT:"proposal for ending the war,"] according to a person familiar with the discussions.
Trump announced the diesel deal while the negotiations were under way, a move Zelenskiy said had caught Kyiv by surprise.
The Ukrainian delegation was headed home on Saturday, presidential aide Dmytro Lytvyn was cited by the Interfax Ukraine news agency as saying.
Putin said after a call with Trump on Friday that an immediate resumption of peace talks was unlikely, citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow.
US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Moscow within the next two weeks, Russian state news agency TASS reported on Saturday, citing a source.
In his remarks at the White House, Trump criticized Zelenskiy over the lack of a peace deal, while demanding an end to Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy facilities.
"I said to him, 'Do what you want. Don't hit refineries. There's plenty of targets. Don't hit refineries.' And he went out and he hit," Trump said. "He better damn well stop."
"I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals, but for some reason he never does," he added.

items.title: インド、ルピー防衛へドル需要抑制　為替ヘッジ規制を強化
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jaspreet Kalra　Nimesh Vora

[ムンバイ １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Jaspreet Kalra　Nimesh Vora

[ムンバイ １０日 ロイター] - インド準備銀行（中央銀行）は１０日、ルピーが過去最安値近辺で推移する中、相場下支えに向け新たな措置を発表した。石油会社のドル調達を直物市場以外に振り向けるとともに、為替ヘッジ規制を強化する。

ルピーは原油価格や世界的な債券利回りの急上昇を背景に下落圧力が続いており、年初来の下落率は７％を超えている。

中銀は国営石油販売会社３社の日々のドル需要を満たす特別窓口を設け、直物市場への圧力を和らげる。

この仕組みでは、中銀が外貨準備から石油会社に直接ドルを供給する。インディアン・オイル、ヒンドゥスタン・ペトロリアム、バーラト・ペトロリアムの３社が１２日から利用可能となる。

ムンバイを拠点とするＡＮＺ銀行の為替ストラテジスト、ディラジ・ニム氏は「石油会社のドル需要に対応することで、為替市場から最大級の需要源の一つが取り除かれ相場変動の抑制につながるだろう。ただ、外貨準備の減少という形で表れることになる」と述べた。

措置の発表後、薄取引の中ルピーはノンデリバラブル・フォワード（ＮＤＦ）市場で対ドルで約０．６％上昇した。

items.title: モンテネグロがロシア軍事ブロガーを国外退去処分　安保上の理由
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ベオグラード ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ベオグラード ９日 ロイター] - モンテネグロの警察と国家保安機関は９日、ロシアの有力な軍事ブログ「ルイバリ」の創設者が同国で逮捕され、他のロシア人３人とともに国家安全保障上の理由で国外追放処分になったと発表した。

地元紙ポビエダが関係筋の話として報じたところによると、ロシア国防省の元職員でもあるミハイル・ズビンチュク氏が、妻を含む他のメンバーとともにアドリア海沿岸の保養地リサンで「ロシアの影響力」を広めた容疑で拘束された。

ルイバリはロシアのウクライナでの戦争を扱うブログの中でも特に人気が高く、１５０万人を超える登録者を持つ。投稿したメッセージで、ズビンチュク氏らは合法的にモンテネグロに滞在し、同国の修道院で撮影する予定だったと説明した。 

首都ポドゴリツァのロシア大使館は、逮捕の理由について説明を求めたと明らかにした。

ルイバリはロシアの幅広い活動を扱うウェブサイトや情報配信網の一部を構成している。

英国は７月、ルイバリに関係する１０人に制裁を科した。ルイバリはロシア政府から支援を受け、「ウクライナに関する虚偽の言説の拡散や、モルドバ、アルメニアを含む欧州の選挙に干渉してきた責任がある」と非難した。 

ロシア政府は、偽情報の拡散や破壊工作展開の疑いを繰り返し否定し、西側が反ロシアのプロパガンダを広めていると主張している。

モンテネグロとロシアの関係は長年、緊張をはらんできた。２０１６年には、モンテネグロ当局がロシアはセルビアの超国家主義者の集団と共謀してクーデターを企てたと非難。ロシア大統領府はこれを否定した。

モンテネグロが１７年に北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）に加盟すると、関係はさらに悪化した。

モンテネグロのスパイッチ首相は今回の逮捕を巡り、同国を不安定化させる試みや、直接的な軍事衝突に至らない行為を指す「ハイブリッド戦」に直面するとの警告があったと述べた。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京 １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[北京 １０日 ロイター] - 中国人力資源・社会保障省は１０日、１─９月の都市部の新規雇用者数が１０５２万人となり、年間目標の８７．７％を達成したと発表した。同省は、サービス業の雇用拡大に向けた新たな措置を計画している。

同省当局者は記者会見で、１─８月の都市部の調査失業率は平均５．２％で、雇用は「おおむね安定」していたと説明した。

李忠次官兼報道官は、他部門と連携しサービス業の発展を通じて雇用を促進する政策文書を策定する方針を示し、サービス業が雇用吸収の主要な受け皿としての機能を一段と発揮できるようにすると述べた。

李氏はまた、労働集約型産業で雇用を安定的に維持するとともに、新興産業や将来有望な産業で新たな雇用機会を模索していくと表明した。

items.title: 台湾は平和重視も自由放棄せず、頼総統が双十節で演説
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Yimou Lee　Ben Blanchard

[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 台湾の頼清徳総統は１０日、双十節（建国記念日）の演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。防衛力の強化は挑発ではないとも強調した。

台湾は防衛費を増額し軍の近代化を進めているが、
items.body:
Yimou Lee　Ben Blanchard

[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 台湾の頼清徳総統は１０日、双十節（建国記念日）の演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。防衛力の強化は挑発ではないとも強調した。

台湾は中国から軍事的・政治的圧力の強化に直面している。中国は一貫して台湾を自国領土と主張しているが、台湾は強く反対している。

台湾は防衛費を増額し軍の近代化を進めているが、 対峙する中国軍の規模ははるかに大きく、ステルス戦闘機や空母、多数のミサイルなどの先進的兵器の配備を進めている。 

頼氏は総統府前で演説し、平和は「願い」だけでは実現できないと強調。 

「台湾は平和を大切にするが、自由を放棄しない。交流には前向きだが、従属は受け入れない」と語った。

また、「権威主義の拡張」に直面する中で、台湾の決意は自らの存続だけに関わるものではないと指摘。

「力がルールに優越することはなく、強者が人々から自らの未来を決める権利を奪うことはできないと、国際社会が今も信じているかどうかの問題だ」と続けた。

防衛投資の拡大については、戦争を挑発するためではなく抑止するためだとして、「対話を放棄するためではなく、対等と尊厳を基礎として対話が行われるようにするために自衛力を強化している」と語った。

頼氏が総統として初めて双十節演説を行った２０２４年の直後、中国は台湾周辺で軍事演習を実施したが、昨年は行わなかった。

台湾周辺で中国が最後に軍事演習を行ったのは昨年１２月下旬で、台湾向けとして過去最大となる１１０億ドル規模の米国の武器売却の報道を受けたものだった。

頼氏は、米国と中国が対話を通じて競争を管理し、紛争や戦争のリスクを低減していることを歓迎すると述べた。

items.title: 米、台湾沖の中国の活動を非難　「著しく安定を損なう」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 米国務省は、台湾東岸沖での中国の海洋活動は「安定を著しく損なう」もので、緊張を悪化させるだけだとの認識を示した。ロイターは先に、８月に同海域で中国の海上民兵船が初めて確認されたと報じていた。

items.body:
[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 米国務省は、台湾東岸沖での中国の海洋活動は「安定を著しく損なう」もので、緊張を悪化させるだけだとの認識を示した。ロイターは先に、８月に同海域で中国の海上民兵船が初めて確認されたと報じていた。

中国は６月以降、沿岸警備隊による定期的な巡視を含め、台湾東岸沖での活動を強化している。

台湾の当局者は、中国が軍、準軍事組織、民間の船舶などを重層的に運用し、海上封鎖の可能性を想定した訓練を行っているとみている。

台湾は、封鎖や有事の際に友好国からの補給ルートとして東岸沖の海域を極めて重要と位置付けている。

米国務省の報道官は、海上民兵の船舶目撃に関する質問に答える形で、米国は台湾東方沖での中国の活動を引き続き懸念していると述べ、「中国の行動は安定を著しく損なうものだ 」と指摘。 

その上で「台湾が７０年以上にわたり平穏に管理してきた海域に対する権限を主張することで中国は緊張を悪化させ、自ら目指すとしている問題の平和的解決を損なっているだけだ」と述べた。 

また、米国は中国政府に対し、台湾への圧力をやめ「台湾の民主的に選出された当局と意義ある対話」を行うよう求めているとした。

中国外務省はコメント要請に応じていない。

items.title: トランプ氏、平和賞逃し批判　「ノルウェーに消えない汚点」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jacob Bogage

[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Jacob Bogage

[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は９日、ノーベル平和賞を受賞できなかったことへの不満を改めて表明し、恥ずべき不名誉な決定でノーベル委員会の本拠地であるノルウェーに汚点を残したと批判した。

委員会は、２０２６年の平和賞を国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）の元判事ナビ・ピレイ氏に授与すると発表した。同氏は、イスラエルがパレスチナ自治区ガザでジェノサイド（集団虐殺）を行ったと結論付けた国連報告書の取りまとめを主導した。

トランプ氏はニューヨーク州シラキュースでの選挙集会で、ピレイ氏を「正体不明の人物」と呼び「その人物のことは聞いたこともない。誰も知らなかった」と述べた。

トランプ氏は大統領就任以来毎年、平和賞を受賞できなかったことに失望を表明してきた。

トランプ氏は「これはノルウェーという国と、こうした不名誉で恥ずべき決定を下した人々にとって、消すことのできない汚点だ」と述べた。

その上で、自ら解決に関与したと主張する複数の紛争を列挙。根拠は示さなかったが、韓国と北朝鮮、日本と北朝鮮、中国と台湾の間での戦争勃発の回避に貢献したと主張した。

「ノーベル平和賞の信用は、反民主主義的で、まさに文明の敵である一握りの過激な思想の持ち主によって永遠に失われた。ノルウェーよ、われわれは忘れない」と述べた。

items.title: サッカー＝マンＣのマレスカ監督がクラブ擁護、「タイトルの価値に傷なし」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［マンチェスター（英国）　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［マンチェスター（英国）　９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、マンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）のエンツォ・マレスカ監督は９日、財務規定違反の問題を抱えている同クラブを擁護した。

マンＣは１１日に行われるプレミアリーグで、先月末に１００件以上の重大な財務規定違反を認定されて以降初の試合となる敵地でのリバプール戦を迎える。クラブはすべての不正行為を否定しており、１日に不服申し立てを行った。

ジョゼップ・グアルディオラ監督の下で３冠を達成した２０２２─２３シーズンにコーチ陣の一員だったマレスカ監督は、リバプール戦に向けた記者会見で、「当時、選手やクラブ、ペップ（グアルディオラ監督）がどれほど努力したか私はよく知っている。だから、その功績を疑う余地など全くない」と語った。また、功績に汚点があると感じるかと問われると、「全くない」と答えた。

６月にグアルディオラ監督の後任として指揮官に就任したマレスカ監督は、契約交渉中に財務規定違反の疑惑に関する話題が上がったことは一度もなかったと明かし、「私はクラブを信頼している。だからこそ、このクラブに加わった。ここ以外に自分がいたいと思うクラブもない。ここにいられることをとても嬉しく思っているし、就任した初日からずっと誇りに感じている」とコメント。就任前に今回の問題の展開を知っていたとしても、「間違いなく」監督職を引き受けていただろうと語った。

items.title: Isaias kills four, about 670,000 without power after landfall
items.author: Rhea Abraham, Rajveer Pardesi, Marianna Parraga
items.creator: Rhea Abraham, Rajveer Pardesi, Marianna Parraga
items.summary: The National Hurricane Center expects storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds and a risk of tornadoes across parts of the US Southeast.
items.body:
Four people died after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday, and about 670,000 residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi were still without power as the storm weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, according to local authorities and electricity monitoring services.
Two of the deaths resulted from trees falling on homes, according to local media and authorities.
Authorities in Florida had received no search and rescue requests shortly after landfall in a sign of limited impact, Governor Ron DeSantis said. But hazardous conditions remained and storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds and a risk of tornadoes across parts of the US Southeast were expected, the National Hurricane Center said.
The tornado threat is expected to continue on Saturday across parts of the Florida Panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas, the NHC said.
In Florida, power restoration was marked as a priority, authorities said, while highways, bridges and airports were reopening, and teams were assessing the damage.
"They're going to make assessments this morning, and I think that'll give us a good sense about the future for the rapidity of the power restoration," DeSantis told a press conference in Tallahassee. Some 16,000 utility linemen had prepared to respond to the storm, he said.
About 420,000 customers in Florida, 190,000 in Alabama, 43,000 in Georgia and 17,000 in Mississippi had no power as of midday Saturday, according to tracking firm PowerOutage.us.
A separate storm on the Pacific Ocean, Rachel, was moving toward the coast of northern Baja California on Saturday, bringing wind gusts and increased tides, which left another 7,000 people without power in California.
Alabama's emergency management agency said the downed trees and power lines made travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning.
"Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X.
A category 2 hurricane when it hit Florida's coast and the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, Isaias is expected to produce gusty winds well inland before weakening below gale force later on Saturday, the NHC said.
On Saturday, oil and gas producer Shell (SHEL.L) said it was beginning to redeploy personnel to its Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox assets in the Gulf, while Chevron (CVX.N) was advancing efforts to redeploy staff to its platforms and seeking to restore full production. "Remobilization of crews will continue through Sunday," it said.
Despite the progress, about 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production in the US Gulf of Mexico remained shut on Saturday, slightly down from Friday numbers, the Marine Minerals Administration said.
Some 113 production platforms representing 30% of the total remained evacuated, according to the agency.
President Donald Trump, asked about hurricane preparations on Friday, told reporters outside the White House that it was "under control." The US Energy Department said on Saturday it authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address supply disruptions due to the hurricane.
Emergency declarations were approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources would be available to respond to Isaias, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X.
"There's also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far, we've had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on," DeSantis told FOX News early on Saturday.
In the coastal city of Pensacola, a lack of drinking water is a problem, the mayor said. Pensacola airport, Florida's 10th largest, was damaged by the storm and is closed to commercial flights until further notice.

items.title: サッカー＝監視対象の選手・関係者の過半数が誹謗中傷受信、ＦＩＦＡ発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 国際サッカー連盟（ＦＩＦＡ）は９日、２０２６年ワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米３カ国大会においてソーシャルメディア保護サービス（ＳＭＰＳ）によって監視された選手、監督、関係者の計１６０６人のうち、半数以上がオンライン上で誹謗中傷を受けていたと発表した。

監視対象となった１６０６人のうち８１２人が、誹謗中傷と分類されるメッセージを少なくとも１件受信した。差別的な誹謗中傷の中で最も多かったのは人種差別に関するもので、誹謗中傷全体の１２％を占めた。一般的な誹謗中傷を除くと、その割合は２０％に上った。

最も標的とされた特定の個人は１万件以上の誹謗中傷投稿を受け取り、そのうち４０％が人種差別的な内容だった。

ＳＭＰＳは１７１０万件の投稿やコメントを分析し、そのうち約２４万件が人の目による精査を経て誹謗中傷であると確認された。２９０５のアカウントについて調査が必要と判断され、７８６アカウントが審査のため法執行機関に報告された。

投稿監視ツールは、ＦＩＦＡおよび加盟協会の公式チャンネルにおける６０７０万件のコメントをスキャンし、スパムを含め９２０万件を非表示にした。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャース山本、リーグ優勝決定Ｓ第2戦で先発へ　初戦はスクバル
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は９日、ブルワーズとのナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）で、１１日の第１戦にタリク・スクバル投手、１２日の第２戦に山本由伸投手を先発させると明らかにした。ＭＬＢ公式サイトが伝えた。

ドジャースはブレーブスとの地区シリーズを３勝１敗で突破。先発したスクバル、ブレーク・スネル、山本、タイラー・グラスノーの４投手は計２１回１／３を投げて自責４、防御率１．６９を記録した。今季のプレーオフ出場チームではレイズの先発陣に次ぐ２番目の好成績となっている。

地区シリーズで第３戦に先発した山本は７回を４安打１失点、１四球、１０三振と好投。中５日で第２戦に登板する予定で、シリーズが第６戦までもつれた場合も通常の登板間隔で先発できる見込み。

山本は昨年のワールドシリーズで最優秀選手（ＭＶＰ）に選出され、最終第７戦では前日の登板から休養なしで救援登板した。今季のプレーオフでも短い登板間隔や救援での起用に応じる意向を示しているが、球団は可能な限り通常の登板間隔を維持する方針。

スネルがリーグ優勝決定シリーズ第３戦、グラスノーが第４戦に先発する可能性がある。ドジャースは昨年まで２年連続でワールドシリーズを制しており、３連覇を目指す。

items.title: Ｆ１＝シンガポールＧＰスプリント予選、フェルスタッペンがトップ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［シンガポール　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［シンガポール　９日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１７戦、シンガポール・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は９日、スプリント予選を行い、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）がトップタイムを記録した。

フェルスタッペンは１分３１秒１５６をマークし、２番手のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）に０秒１２０差をつけた。シンガポールでは過去に、ポールポジション（ＰＰ）獲得も優勝もともに経験していなかった。

フェルスタッペンは「ソフトタイヤを装着すると、マシンが少し生き返ったように感じた。トップになれるとは予想していなかったので、とてもうれしい」とコメントした。

３番手はシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）。総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）は７番手だった。

ラッセルは同日のフリー走行でトップタイムを記録したが、パワーユニットの部品交換に伴い、１１日の決勝では計４０グリッド降格のペナルティーを受ける。ただ、１０日のスプリントには影響しない。

スプリント予選の最初のセッションでは、セルヒオ・ペレス（メキシコ、キャデラック）が防護壁に衝突し、コース上に破片が散乱したため赤旗中断となった。その後、計時システムの不具合で第２セッションの開始が遅れたほか、追い抜き支援機能の作動にも問題が発生した。

items.title: India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest
items.author: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Sakshi Dayal
items.creator: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Sakshi Dayal
items.summary: Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a rally organized by the Cockroach movement.
items.body:
Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and the founder of the "Cockroach" youth movement in Delhi on Saturday as security forces [USN:L1N45V075 TEXT:"locked down"] parts of the capital to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India's election chief.
Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the city, mobile internet services were suspended in the central business district and dozens of metro stations and markets were shut as authorities moved to stop a demonstration organised by the Cockroach movement.
The protest was aimed at Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say disproportionately benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The movement had planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, but the area was sealed off by security forces before the demonstration began.
A home ministry official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters more than 2,000 people were detained in Delhi. Local media said about 400 protesters were held in India's financial hub, Mumbai.
There was no immediate comment from police on the detentions.
The United Nations human rights office expressed concerns over mass detentions before and during the protests.
"We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled," UN Human Rights Spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan said in a statement.
He also urged authorities to engage in "meaningful dialogue" to address the "broadly held" concerns expressed.
The Indian mission to the UN in Geneva, however, called the UN's concerns "misplaced" and said they constitute "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."
It stressed that the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by India's Constitution. "As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order," the statement added.
MOVEMENT LEADERS HELD Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka when their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi, the group said in a statement.
Television footage showed Dipke challenging officers who approached him on board the aircraft.
"I have come to be arrested, arrest me ... I am not afraid of you guys," he said.
"No, this is not an arrest," one officer replied. "Please cooperate."
The movement condemned what it called the "authoritarian detention" of its leaders, demanded their release and vowed to continue protesting.
"We will continue our protest tomorrow, day after ... until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. We will be on the streets," CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde told reporters.
CJP also said authorities refused to provide updates on the leaders' whereabouts or health, even after news arrived of the death of Dipke's grandmother. Police said Dipke was informed of her death and was offered help to return home for the funeral.
Some opposition lawmakers and former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee of West Bengal, Arvind Kejriwal of Delhi, and Pinarayi Vijayan of Kerala were also detained, TV channels showed.
Representatives of two digital news outlets said police briefly detained four of their reporters while they were covering the demonstrations. A Reuters journalist was also detained briefly before being released.
Across the capital of about 20 million people, security forces set up checkpoints on major roads and entry points, boarded buses searching for protesters and inspected vehicles. Barricades and concrete blocks disrupted traffic while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear-gas launchers guarded key routes.
NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The demonstrations represent one of the most serious tests yet for Modi, stemming from allegations that election authorities improperly revised voter rolls ahead of recent state polls.
Protests intensified after the Indian Express reported last week that two election commissioners had questioned Kumar's voter-list revisions that removed roughly 130 million names from voter lists.
Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied allegations of wrongdoing.
The BJP says its electoral success reflects Modi's popularity and India's economic growth, and accuses opposition parties of spreading misinformation.
The near [USN:L6N45U0IF TEXT:"daily protests"] come just months after demonstrations over exam paper leaks forced his [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"education minister to quit"].
The unrest also comes ahead of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027.
Rahul Gandhi, leader of the main opposition Congress party, said Modi's opponents would not back down.
A senior BJP member, Ravi Shankar Prasad, said the party was not opposed to demonstrations but the street protests had been "weaponised" by rivals due to election defeats.
DELETIONS AFFECTED STATE POLLS, OPPOSITION ALLEGES Opposition parties say the deletions affected the outcome of recent state elections won by the BJP and have cast a shadow over voting in the world's largest democracy.
Election Commission data show about 130 million voter entries were removed during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated, 30 million who could not be traced and 28 million who had died.
The commission says the removals relate to entries identified during the draft revision process and that any eligible voter incorrectly deleted can re-enrol.

items.title: ＮＢＡ＝レブロン、シクサーズでのプレシーズン初戦で10得点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のセブンティシクサーズに加入したレブロン・ジェームズ（４１）は８日、ネッツとのプレシーズン戦で移籍後初出場を果たし、１０得点５アシストを記録した。

レブロンはフィールドゴールの試投がわずか１本だったものの、フリースロー８本を全て成功させた。プレーしたのは前半のみで後半は出場せず、シクサーズは１０８─１１４で敗れた。

レブロンは試合後、「新しいユニホームを着ていたのは確かだが、バスケットボールはバスケットボール。コート上でプレーするものだ」と語り、これまで練習でともに汗を流してきたチームメートと実戦に臨めたことを喜んだ。

レブロンは７月、フリーエージェント（ＦＡ）として２年総額８００万ドル（約１２億７０００万円）、選手オプション付きの契約で加入。昨季はレーカーズで６０試合に出場し、１試合平均２０．９得点６．１リバウンド７．２アシストを記録した。

オールスター選出２２回を誇るレブロンは、通算出場試合数（１６２２）と通算得点（４万３４４０）でＮＢＡ歴代最多記録を保持。ヒートで２回、キャバリアーズとレーカーズで各１回、ＮＢＡ制覇を果たしている。

佐野が先発したＰＳＶは前半２９分、右サイドからのクロスを相手ＧＫが弾くと、これをフース・ティルが頭で押し込んで先制。後半２３分にはＣＫから相手のオウンゴールを誘発した。佐野はフル出場した。

items.title: ゴルフ＝米沢が20位、松山は30位に後退　ベイカレントクラシック
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフの秋季シリーズ、ベイカレント・クラシック・レクサスは９日、神奈川県横浜ＣＣ（パー７１）で第２ラウンドを行い、米沢蓮が日本勢最高の２０位につけた。

前日１７位の米沢は４バーディー、２ボギーの６９で回り、通算５アンダーの１３７。１２位スタートの松山英樹は３バーディー、４ボギーの７２とスコアを落とし、通算３アンダーの３０位に後退した。

同じく１２位で出た久常涼は７１で回り、通算４アンダーの１３８で２６位。金谷拓実と砂川公佑は３０位、岩田寛と石坂友宏は３８位、藤本佳則と細野勇策は４６位、香妻陣一朗は５４位、中島啓太は６１位、岩崎亜久竜は６３位、アマチュアの長崎煌心は７０位だった。

首位には通算１１アンダーでキース・ミッチェルとジェーコブ・ブリッジマン（ともに米国）が並んだ。ミッチェルは８バーディー、２ボギーの６５で６つ伸ばし、ブリッジマンは４バーディー、１ボギーの６８で回った。

CARACAS, Oct 9 : Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has authorized Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, to operate in the Latin American country.
The authorization is part of an agreement with the US firm, the Venezuelan government said in a statement on Friday.
The company's satellite-internet unit has continued to expand its global subscriber base, aided by launches of additional satellites and a growing range of consumer, enterprise, aviation, maritime and government services.

items.title: サッカー＝2位リヨンがランスに屈し初黒星、中村は途中出場
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ランス（フランス）　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ランス（フランス）　９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのフランス１部は９日、１試合を行い、２位リヨンは敵地でＲＣランスに１─２で敗れ、今季初黒星を喫した。リヨンの中村敬斗は後半１５分から途中出場した。

リヨンは前後半に１点ずつ奪われて２点のビハインドを背負ったが、後半３９分に相手が退場者を出して数的優位に立つと、直後に１９歳カリス・メラが相手守備陣のミスを突いて１点を返した。しかし、反撃もそこまでで、開幕からの無敗が途絶えた。

リヨンは勝ち点１１で暫定２位。一方、ＲＣランスは同７とし、１５位から暫定７位に浮上した。

items.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、坂本が3回戦進出　ジョコビッチは敗退
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［上海　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［上海　９日　ロイター］ - テニスのマスターズ上海大会は９日、男子シングルス２回戦を行い、予選勝者の坂本怜が第２３シードでロシア出身のアンドレイ・ルブレフを６─４、６─４のストレートで破り、３回戦進出を果たした。

世界ランキング１３７位の坂本は第１セットの第１ゲームでブレークに成功。第２セットも第９ゲームで相手のサービスゲームを破り、元世界５位の格上選手から金星を挙げた。３回戦では第９シードのアレックス・デミノー（オーストラリア）と対戦する。

過去４回優勝の第１０シード、ノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）はフベルト・フルカチュ（ポーランド）に４─６、３─６で敗れ、初戦で姿を消した。

ジョコビッチはこれまでフルカチュとの対戦で８戦全勝だった。試合後、「北京でプレーしていた時の状態には程遠かった。少し疲れていて、フレッシュではなかった」と振り返った。

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 9 : Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.
Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents. 
The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change.
Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.

Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones. 
The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said.
Nuvacore declined to comment.
The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021.
Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned.
Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand.
Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.
Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts.
Shares in both companies have risen more than 180 per cent this year.
Nvidia launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to sell $20 billion worth of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

Oct 9 : Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson.

items.title: 米欧・ウクライナが和平案協議　米ロ軽油合意と同日
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン　９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン　９日 ロイター] - 米国、ウクライナ、欧州の交渉担当者が９日、マイアミでウクライナ戦争終結に向けた統一提案での合意を目指し、６時間にわたる協議を行った。協議に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

匿名を条件に語った同関係者によると、今後数週間で案をまとめてロシアに提示し、冬を迎える前に事態の打開を図ることを目指している。

同日、トランプ米大統領は、燃料価格の引き下げに向けてロシアが世界市場にディーゼル（軽油）を供給することで合意したと発表。米政権は、ロシアの戦費となる収入を断つために課していたロシア産燃料への制裁を解除した。この合意は米議員やウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領から批判を浴びた。 

ゼレンスキー氏は声明で「資金は全て、人々に対する、ウクライナに対する、そしてわれわれ全員に対する戦争に使われる。わが交渉チームは単に目くらましに使われているに過ぎないと考えている。それは決して公正ではない」と述べた。

ロシアのプーチン大統領はトランプ氏との電話会談後、ウクライナによるモスクワへのドローン攻撃を理由に、和平協議を直ちに再開する可能性は低いとの見方を示した。

マイアミでの協議には米国のウィットコフ、クシュナー両特使とウクライナ代表団のほか、欧州と北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の代表者が出席した。

関係者によると、交渉担当者は幅広い議題について話し合った。その中には、米国と欧州による安全保障の確約を含むウクライナ向けの戦後パッケージも含まれた。

また、ウクライナ向けの戦後経済計画や、欧州連合（ＥＵ）加盟に向けた道筋についても協議された。

ただ関係者は、センシティブな問題として、領土を巡る「幾つかのアイデア」も議論されたとしたが、詳細には立ち入らなかった。

今後の平和な時代の土台となる、欧州とロシアの安全保障体制についても議論された。関係者は詳細には触れなかった。

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 9 : Amazon on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its first tablet computers featuring the voice assistant.
Daniel Rausch, a 17-year Amazon veteran who has served as vice president of Alexa and Echo for over three years, is stepping away from the unit next month, Amazon said in response to a Reuters inquiry.
Rausch, who has served as the face of Alexa at events and global launches, will return in another capacity in the devices and services division in 2027.
In his place, Amazon will install Aidan Marcuss, currently the vice president of Fire TV, advertising and the Amazon appstore. Marcuss joined Amazon from Microsoft in early 2025. He oversaw the release of a new Fire TV stick last month, which has garnered mixed reviews.

Alexa has been a consistent money-loser for Amazon since its release in 2014.
Amazon spent several years developing a new version of the voice assistant offering generative AI that can respond to longer prompts. The service is featured in the new Alexa Tablets announced on Thursday that Amazon has priced as a high-end product compared with prior Fire tablets that were inexpensive.
Alexa+, as the latest version is known, is included in the $139-per-year Prime membership or for $20 monthly as a standalone service.
